target.title: feat(gateway): add ticketed read-only MCP App host
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

Closes #109851

## Summary

- Add a generic standalone MCP App host that exchanges a short-lived signed view ticket instead of exposing the operator Gateway bearer token.
- Keep the trusted shell on the Gateway origin and reuse the separate static sandbox listener; no view secret or dynamic app data enters the listener document.
- Keep the standalone host deliberately read-only and add one official `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` fixture that drives both the existing authenticated Control UI host and the new standalone host over the real browser/transport path.

## What Problem This Solves

Future channel and standalone browser launches need to render one MCP App view without handing the page a reusable operator credential. The existing authenticated Control UI host is not a least-privilege launch boundary for an external browser surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process-local HMAC capability is bound to the current OpenClaw session key, MCP runtime session, view id, and view-lease deadline. The new HTTP boundary reconstructs only that live view, while the static host implements the stable MCP Apps initialization, ping, input/result, sizing, and teardown messages and rejects tool/resource requests.

This reuses the existing MCP runtime, view lease, sandbox proxy, and Gateway configuration. It adds no config/env surface, protocol version, channel launch UX, approval flow, or privileged capability.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, an authenticated Gateway client can obtain a standalone URL for the current view and open it without exposing the Gateway bearer token. Existing Control UI behavior is unchanged. There is no new default UI or channel action in this PR.

## Independent Landing and Backward Safety

- Existing `mcp.app.view` fields and semantics are preserved. `standaloneUrl` and its expiry are optional additions; ticket capacity, expiry races, or unexpected issuance failures omit those fields while returning the original successful view payload.
- The two new HTTP paths exist only behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Disabled installations and all other routes retain current behavior.
- The standalone URL is fully functional on this PR alone: initialize, ping, input/result delivery, read-only denials, reload, teardown, and rejection states require no later MCP Apps PR.
- The existing Control UI keeps its current app-only tool/resource authority. The conformance fixture proves shared/app-only tools and app resources remain available there while model-only tools remain denied.
- No current UI consumes the optional standalone field, and no current capability advertisement changes.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: the new route and optional Gateway response field are additive behind the existing MCP Apps gate. No launch button, channel integration, approval UI, tool/resource capability, or later-PR contract is advertised. A later PR may expose the already-working URL in channel UX, but is not required for any behavior enabled here.

## Evidence

- Real transport/browser path: an official self-contained `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.4` app ran through a real stdio MCP server, Gateway WebSocket authentication, Control UI Vite host, Gateway HTTP routes, static sandbox listener, and nested postMessage transports.
- Both hosts completed the stable `2026-01-26` initialize handshake and standard MCP `ping`, then received the original tool input and result.
- Control UI baseline: server tool/resource capabilities were advertised; the app-only companion tool and app resource succeeded; a model-only tool was denied.
- Standalone boundary: neither server tools nor server resources were advertised; tool and resource calls were denied; the only authorization header was `MCP-App v1...`, never `Bearer test`.
- Lifecycle: app-requested teardown removed the frame, reload reconstructed it, and a second load received the original result.
- Ticket security: unit/integration coverage rejects tampered, expired, wrong-session, wrong-runtime, wrong-view, replaced-view, and inappropriate reuse states; the browser scenario proves tampered and expired URLs fail.
- Origin/CSP review: the shell is static on the Gateway origin, the iframe is restricted to the exact separate sandbox origin, the listener stays static, the ticket remains in the URL fragment and is sent only in the dedicated authorization header, responses are no-store/no-referrer, and the shell never receives the Gateway token.
- Two final full-branch autoreviews after simplification/fixes reported no actionable findings. A reviewer-found missing standard `ping` response was fixed and exercised in both host modes before the clean final pass.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` — full runtime and Control UI production build passed, including plugin SDK export and Control UI performance gates.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed with the frozen lockfile.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/e2e/mcp-app-conformance.e2e.test.ts` — 13 gateway assertions and the complete Chromium conformance scenario passed.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` — passed.
- Repeated canonical-base updates were rebased without conflicts; every final `git range-diff` showed all three commits patch-identical. The push used a fresh `upstream/main` fetch and verified ancestry immediately before publication.
- Blacksmith Testbox passed the build and broad static gates before exposing two strict fixture type errors that were fixed. Two later Testbox leases failed during delegated file sync before executing code, so trusted-source exact-head fallback proof ran in isolated temporary clones with frozen dependencies.

## Simplification and Scope

The PR is six files: three production files plus two focused Gateway tests and one maintained browser fixture. Net production growth is 463 LOC. Most of that is the single standalone module owning the capability store, HTTP/security boundary, static shell, and minimal protocol bridge; keeping those concerns together avoids a new public abstraction or duplicated policy. The remaining production additions are narrow route and optional-response wiring. No cleanup, config, launch UI, or privileged capability is mixed in.

## Known Gaps

- This does not add channel launch UX, approval UI, or standalone tool/resource authority.
- Tickets are intentionally process-local and expire no later than the view lease; a Gateway restart invalidates them.
- At the bounded live-ticket capacity, existing view responses continue to work but omit a standalone URL until capacity expires.
- Required GitHub CI on the published head remains the final landing gate.

target.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite startup falls back to the system `mount` command when `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unavailable. That synchronous probe had no deadline, so a stalled `mount` process could block state or plugin database initialization indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback probe now has a one-second hard timeout. If filesystem classification times out, SQLite conservatively uses rollback journaling instead of assuming WAL is safe. Existing behavior for successful mount classification and non-timeout probe failures is preserved.

## User Impact

Database-backed OpenClaw startup no longer waits indefinitely on a wedged mount probe. When the deadline is reached, startup continues with rollback journaling, avoiding both the hang and an unsafe WAL assumption for an unclassified network filesystem.

## Evidence

- Regression-first tests cover the missing timeout and the conservative timeout policy.
- Before: the production `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` path with an isolated stalled `mount` fixture exceeded a 4-second external guard (`exit_status=124`).
- After: the same production path returned in about 1.0 seconds, selected `journal_mode=delete`, and exited successfully.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts` on Node 24.15.0: 38 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts`: passed.
- Type-aware oxlint and TypeScript checking for the affected files: passed.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: no actionable findings after the conservative rollback follow-up.

Not exercised: a real macOS/BSD host or a real network filesystem. The live proof used the production SQLite configuration call path with a test-only local command fixture.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and any-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that (1) heading checks block valid headingless skills, (2) any-line overlap is trivially bypassable — a plan document sharing a single heading or boilerplate line receives `requiresExplicitApproval=false` and overwrites the skill, and (3) zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser, rejects empty bodies, and uses a **substantial-continuity classifier** that requires at least 3 shared non-heading body lines AND at least 50% of original non-heading content retained before allowing automatic apply. Low-continuity updates force pending approval even under `auto` policy, preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites while blocking incidental-overlap plans that share only headings or 1-2 boilerplate lines.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Low-continuity update proposals (insufficient shared content with current SKILL.md) are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Substantially continuous updates (≥3 shared non-heading lines, ≥50% original content retained) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid headingless skill updates apply normally when they retain substantial content
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The low-continuity approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for low-continuity updates while substantially continuous updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`**

**Live approval-hook proof (terminal transcript from exact head)**:

The `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` function is the approval hook that determines whether an agent-initiated `apply` action proceeds automatically or requires operator approval. Under `auto` policy, it returns `undefined` (no approval required) for actions that pass all checks. For low-continuity updates, it returns `requireApproval` with a warning prompt, which blocks the agent from applying the proposal until the operator approves. SKILL.md remains unchanged until approval is granted.

```console
=== Approval-Hook Real Behavior Proof ===
SHA: e0dc28d1ea33
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T10:15:40.062Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Low-continuity update blocked by approval hook (auto policy) ---
SKILL.md before proposal:
  ---
  name: weather
  description: Weather skill
  ---
  
  # Weather
  
  Steps to check weather.
  Check the forecast.
  Save the result.

Approval hook result: requireApproval (BLOCKED)
  title: "Apply workspace skill proposal"
  severity: "warning"
  allowedDecisions: ["allow-once","deny"]
SKILL.md unchanged after approval hook block: true

--- Proof 2: Incidental heading-only overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 3: Incidental 1-line overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 4: Incidental 2-line overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 5: Substantial continuity update allowed (auto policy) ---
Approval hook result: undefined (ALLOWED)

--- Proof 6: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged after rejection: true

=== Summary ===
1. Low-continuity update: approval hook returns requireApproval, SKILL.md unchanged ✅
2. Heading-only overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
3. 1-line overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
4. 2-line overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
5. Substantial continuity: approval hook returns undefined (allowed) ✅
6. Empty body: hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged ✅
```

**Substantial-continuity classifier detail** (exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`):

```console
Original SKILL.md body (non-heading lines):
  "Steps to check weather.", "Check the forecast.", "Save the result." (3 lines)

Heading-only overlap (shares "# Weather" heading, no non-heading overlap):
  overlapCount=0, ratio=0.0 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

1-line overlap (shares "Steps to check weather.", 1/3=33%):
  overlapCount=1, ratio=0.33 → 1<3 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

2-line overlap (shares "Steps to check weather." + "Check the forecast.", 2/3=67%):
  overlapCount=2, ratio=0.67 → 2<3 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

Substantial continuity (shares 4/6 non-heading lines, 67%):
  overlapCount=4, ratio=0.67 → 4≥3 && 0.67≥0.5 → isSubstantialContinuity=true
  → requiresExplicitApproval=false, auto-apply proceeds ✅
```

**Unit tests (exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`)**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts (35 tests) 13380ms
 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts (3 tests) 4269ms
     ✓ gates low-continuity updates with requiresExplicitApproval and rejects empty bodies  1749ms
     ✓ gates incidental-overlap plans that share only a heading or few non-heading lines  1678ms
     ✓ applies headingless and substantially continuous updates without requiresExplicitApproval  841ms
 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts (9 tests) 1531ms
     ✓ requires approval for low-continuity updates under auto policy  1019ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  47 passed (47)
```

**Validation matrix**:

```
Proposal body form                                        => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                              => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)               => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Zero shared non-heading lines (complete rewrite/unrelated) => requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental heading-only overlap (plan shares heading)     => requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental 1-line overlap (plan shares one non-heading)   => requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental 2-line overlap (plan shares two non-heading)   => requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Substantial continuity (≥3 lines, ≥50% retained)          => requiresExplicitApproval=false, auto-apply proceeds
Valid headingless skill with substantial content          => requiresExplicitApproval=false, auto-apply proceeds
```

**CI note**: The `startup-memory` check failure (`status --json` median RSS exceeding 425 MB limit) and the `format` check failure (`test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`) are pre-existing issues on the `main` branch, not introduced by this PR. All other CI checks passed.

target.title: fix #95351: [Feature]: Generic JSONL line-parsing hook for CliBackendPlugin (native tool-card support beyond claude-stream-json)
target.body:
Fixes #95351

## What Problem This Solves

- Affected surface / workflow: Plugin-registered CLI backends that declare `output: "jsonl"` and stream provider-specific JSONL lines into OpenClaw's CLI runner/parser path.
- Root cause, in product terms: The source-of-truth parser contract for generic plugin CLI JSONL output lived only inside OpenClaw's built-in Claude/Gemini stream dialect handling. `CliBackendPlugin` exposed runtime hooks for command setup, but no public parser hook was preserved through backend resolution and consumed by the JSONL runner, so third-party CLIs could not map already-executed native tool activity or reasoning text into OpenClaw's existing display/thinking lanes without impersonating a built-in dialect. The review follow-up root cause was that the new normalized `thinking` event initially mapped to optional commentary instead of the existing thinking stream.
- Why it matters / User impact: Plugin authors can now integrate native JSONL CLIs while keeping provider-specific wire parsing inside the plugin and still get OpenClaw native tool-card rendering and thinking output. Existing users keep the same defaults because the hook is opt-in and attached only to plugin-owned backend registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Fix classification: Root cause fix, contingent on maintainer sponsorship for the new public plugin SDK hook direction.
- Complete shipped solution: Add optional `CliBackendPlugin.parseJsonlEvent(line, ctx)` support, preserve that hook through CLI backend resolution/execution, invoke it from the JSONL stdout parser before built-in fallback parsing, and normalize plugin events into existing assistant text, `stream: "thinking"`, result/session/usage, and display-only native tool-card event paths. The branch is replayed on current `origin/main`; latest drift check reports `has_conflicts=false`, `sync_main_required=false`, and merge base equals current `origin/main`.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The patch adds the missing canonical parser contract at the plugin boundary and routes normalized events at the same source parser boundary where OpenClaw already converts CLI stdout into UI/runtime streams. It fixes the ownership gap and the thinking-event mapping gap directly instead of adding downstream text heuristics, a provider-specific special case, or a trusted-delivery shortcut.
- Key design boundary / source of truth: Contract surface is the public plugin SDK `CliBackendPlugin` type and normalized plugin JSONL event union; the canonical source of truth is the plugin-owned parser hook plus OpenClaw's CLI JSONL parser boundary. Plugin code owns provider-specific wire format parsing; OpenClaw owns normalized assistant/thinking/display projections and keeps tool execution authority separate from display projection.
- Non-goals / what did not change: This does not change the `agents.defaults.cliBackends.*.jsonlDialect` config schema, add a new built-in dialect value, execute plugin-reported tools through OpenClaw's tool catalog, let plugin display events count as message delivery/source-reply evidence, change sandbox or permission enforcement, or change Claude/Gemini stream-json semantics.

target.title: fix(sqlite): add 10s SIGKILL timeout to mount lookup during WAL safety check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readMountEntries()` in `sqlite-wal.ts` invokes `childProcess.execFileSync("mount", [])` without a timeout. On systems with unresponsive NFS/SMB mounts, the `mount` command can hang indefinitely, blocking the SQLite WAL safety check during startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing try-catch guards against execution failures, but cannot guard against a hung process. Adding `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the lookup is bounded (10s) and the process is forcibly terminated on timeout, matching the repository pattern used in `src/cli/ports.ts`, `src/tui/tui.ts`, and `src/daemon/program-args.ts`.

## Evidence

35/37 sqlite-wal tests pass (2 pre-existing failures due to SQLite version in test environment):

```
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  2 failed | 35 passed (37)
```

The change is a pure safety improvement — the existing catch block returns `[]` on failure, and the new options only add a time bound to an otherwise unbounded synchronous call.

## Merge Risk

Low — single-file change, nothing added to the public API surface. The function already has an empty-array fallback in its catch block, so the timeout path degrades gracefully.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users can see a parent turn as idle while tracked subagents are still running. The source message provides no compact indication of concurrent child work or terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now emits one generic typed `subagent_progress` presentation event with source-message provenance. The Discord plugin maps that portable event to typing plus one count reaction, and retains a red reaction after a non-OK child outcome. One opt-in switch, `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, controls the behavior; emoji, cadence, and the one-hour typing bound remain internal defaults.

The maintainer rewrite deliberately keeps transport policy in Discord, routes native and tracked ACP spawns through the same core lifecycle, and persists only Discord reaction ownership and terminal outcome in plugin SQLite. Durable rows make count cleanup and failure presentation retry-safe across response loss and gateway restart without blocking subagent lifecycle delivery. Progress runtime code remains behind its own lazy import so the public Discord API and unrelated subagent hooks do not increase lightweight CLI startup memory.

## User Impact

When enabled, the Discord source message shows `1️⃣` through `🔟` as tracked child concurrency changes, removes the count after the final child ends, keeps typing active for up to one hour, and leaves `🔴` for error, timeout, or killed outcomes. target.title: fix: keep session thinking through transcript recovery
target.body:
Closes #109275

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with stored `/think` or `/verbose` session preferences could lose those preferences when command-session resolution rotates the OpenClaw session id for terminal transcript-registry recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps stored thinking and verbose preferences available when terminal transcript recovery creates a replacement session id but the configured daily/idle reset policy would otherwise still treat the session as current. It intentionally does not carry those preferences when terminal recovery overlaps a configured daily or idle reset boundary, so a configured clean-session reset still wins.

## User Impact

Users who set `/think high` or `/verbose full` keep that session preference through terminal transcript recovery instead of silently falling back to defaults. Operators who rely on daily or idle session resets still get a clean session without inherited thinking or verbose preferences.

target.title: fix: timed-out agent runs no longer retain MCP processes
target.body:
Related: #92569

Follow-up to #93559.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an embedded agent run that times out while its MCP catalog is still starting can leave its run lease alive. The command lane continues, but stale MCP processes can remain pinned after the abandoned run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command queue now invokes a synchronous timeout hook before admitting later work, and a materialized MCP run registers an idempotent disposer immediately after lease acquisition. ## User Impact

Timed-out or cancellation-resistant agent runs no longer retain their MCP run lease indefinitely. MCP calls already in flight may finish normally, and unrelated request or app-view leases remain active.

target.title: fix(discord): honor caller abortSignal during 429 retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`requestDiscord` in `extensions/discord/src/api.ts` retries 429 responses with a backoff driven by `retryAsync`. The caller's `options.signal` is honored by the fetch itself (merged into the per-attempt request signal), but the sleep between attempts used the default unabortable timer. With `retry_after` up to 60s (and `maxDelayMs` at 5 minutes), an aborted caller still waited out the full backoff and then issued one more request whose result would be discarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryAsync` accepts a custom `sleep`; this passes `sleepWithAbort(ms, options?.signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` — the same abort-aware helper adopted for retry backoffs in sibling fixes (#109604 telegram startup probe, #108561 discord gateway READY retry, #108408 feishu comment reply retry). When the signal fires mid-backoff, the sleep's abort rejection propagates through `retryAsync` and rejects `requestDiscord` immediately, mirroring how an abort during the fetch itself surfaces. Without a signal, `sleepWithAbort` degenerates to a plain ref'd timer, so existing callers that pass no `signal` see zero behavior change.

## Changes

- Pass an abort-aware `sleep` to `retryAsync` in `requestDiscord`, wired to `options.signal`.
- Add a regression test: a stub fetcher that always returns 429 with `retry_after: 30`, an abort fired 200ms into the backoff; asserts the request rejects promptly with an abort error and the fetcher is called exactly once.

## User Impact

Callers that cancel Discord API work (plugin shutdown, gateway teardown, aborted operations) now stop promptly during 429 rate-limit backoffs instead of sleeping up to the full `retry_after`/cap and issuing a doomed extra request.

## Evidence

Exact head: `05d2676197d64654f66374da3f59e577ad7ec1cb`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  18 passed (18)
```

Same focused suite with the change stashed: the new test waits out two full 30s backoffs (`tests 63.72s`) and fails the promptness assertion. With the fix it rejects ~200ms after the abort fires.

`oxlint` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions test project reports no errors in discord files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- `timeoutMs` remains a per-attempt request timeout and intentionally does not bound backoff sleeps; the caller signal is the cancellation path.
- No change to retry counts, delay caps, or Retry-After honoring.

target.title: fix(feishu): honor abortSignal during app registration poll interval
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pollAppRegistration` in `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` accepts an `abortSignal` and checks it at the top of each poll iteration, but the interval sleep between polls runs on a bare timer. When the signal fires mid-interval, the loop keeps sleeping through the full remaining interval — which `slow_down` responses keep raising by 5s at a time — before the abort is noticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The interval helper now sleeps via `sleepWithAbort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, the same abort-aware helper recently adopted for retry backoffs in sibling plugins (#109604 telegram startup probe, #108561 discord gateway READY retry, #108408 feishu comment reply retry). The abort rejection is swallowed inside the helper so the loop's existing top-of-iteration `aborted` check remains the single exit path and the `PollOutcome` contract (resolve with `{ status: "timeout" }`, never throw) stays unchanged.

Note: the only in-tree caller today (the `runScanToCreate` setup wizard) does not pass a signal. This change completes the function's existing public contract so the `abortSignal` parameter is honored everywhere it is already accepted — the bare interval sleep was the one remaining gap next to the loop's own `aborted` check.

## Changes

- Thread `abortSignal` into `sleepRegistrationPollInterval` at both call sites (transient-error path and normal path) and sleep via `sleepWithAbort`.
- Add a regression test: a stub fetch that always returns `authorization_pending`, a 30s poll interval, and an abort fired 200ms in; asserts the poll resolves `{ status: "timeout" }` promptly and issues no second poll request.

## User Impact

Callers that cancel app registration polling (setup teardown, plugin lifecycle shutdown) now stop promptly instead of waiting out the remaining poll interval — which `slow_down` responses can raise well beyond the default 5s.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3a8cc1e61d756a62cb6d1cd9b9cbb12fa9c8e144`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Same focused suite with the old bare-`sleep` helper (change stashed): the new test only returns after the full 30s interval (`tests 30.13s`) and fails the promptness assertion. With the fix it resolves ~200ms after the abort fires.

`oxlint` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions test project reports no errors in feishu files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- In-flight registration POSTs keep their existing 10s `APP_REGISTRATION_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` budget; aborting an active request is unchanged.
- No change to the poll interval or the `slow_down` escalation policy.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

```console
# Active descendant check: countActiveDescendantRuns() smoke test
$ node --import tsx -e "import { countActiveDescendantRuns } from './src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts'; console.log('empty key:', countActiveDescendantRuns(''), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('unknown key:', countActiveDescendantRuns('no-such'), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('All returned 0 without throwing ✅');"
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch and uses the shared `hasErrnoCode(err, "ENOENT")` helper from `src/infra/errors.ts` to detect the missing-file case. This reuses the canonical errno guard instead of duplicating the `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code` cast across three readers, keeping error classification on the shared contract. It then throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged. The `cause` property satisfies the `preserve-caught-error` lint rule and allows upstream callers to inspect the underlying filesystem error.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 156/156 passing (includes 3 ENOENT regression tests covering all 3 command paths)

- `git diff --check` — clean

### Real CLI proof (via `pnpm openclaw`)

**Command 1: `config set --batch-file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config set --batch-file /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 2: `config patch --file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config patch --file /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
Error: --file not found: /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 3: `secrets apply --from`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json | ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/nonexistent/path/plan.json' | ENOENT. Re-run openclaw secrets apply --from <path> --dry-run to inspect the plan without writing.
```

target.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale encrypted reasoning failures
target.body:
fix #95441

Related: #95493
Related: #95587

AI-assisted: yes (GitHub Copilot).

## What Problem This Solves

Persisted GitHub Copilot reasoning can become invalid when OpenClaw reconstructs a session, causing `invalid_encrypted_content` or a missing reply on a later turn. The rejection can happen while creating a Responses request or after its SSE stream opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses the existing owner boundaries:

- **Cold replay history:** the GitHub Copilot provider's `sanitizeReplayHistory` hook removes persisted thinking/reasoning when a Copilot Responses `AgentSession` is rehydrated. The sanitized history becomes that session's in-memory state, while reasoning generated later in the same agent/tool loop remains available.
- **Active wire payload:** the provider boundary preserves complete native `rs_*` reasoning, converts Copilot connection-bound reasoning IDs to idless replay, keeps already-idless reasoning, and removes foreign, malformed, or incomplete reasoning. Existing message/function-call ID normalization remains intact.
- **Single bounded recovery:** Responses request creation and SSE draining share one retry budget. Before any public model output, a recognized encrypted-content failure retries once after removing only the top-level `encrypted_content` field from reasoning items. The retry preserves reasoning summaries and IDs, assistant messages, function calls, function outputs, and their order. Requests containing compaction fail closed instead of dropping compaction or constructing an item without its required ciphertext.

This separates prevention from recovery because neither is sufficient alone. Applying only a broad replay policy would discard valid same-loop continuity; relying only on recovery would keep sending known-stale state and make provider failure part of the normal path. Provider-owned cold sanitation plus one bounded generic fallback avoids both without adding session state, configuration, or a compatibility path.

The change adds no configuration, persisted replay state, transcript mutation, or public SDK surface.

## User Impact

Rehydrated Copilot sessions no longer send persisted opaque reasoning. Valid same-loop reasoning and tool continuation remain available. If a provider rejects stale reasoning before output starts, recovery preserves the continuation structure; compaction remains untouched and fails closed.

## Upstream Behavior References

- [`@github/copilot@1.0.69-2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot/v/1.0.69-2), build `546d22a58d`: active history retains encrypted reasoning, while cold resume, abort/cancel, and effective-model history rewrite strip opaque reasoning.
- [`github/copilot-sdk@5adb51b`](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/5adb51b9e2ac50ad4876e756fa8c05549c1490fd/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts#L1044-L1054) documents OpenAI encrypted reasoning as session-bound and stripped on resume.
- [`microsoft/vscode@47657de`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L145-L172) requests `reasoning.encrypted_content`; its [history selection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L306-L395) excludes pre-marker history, and its [serializer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L631-L660) replays only complete Responses reasoning.
- OpenAI Node `6.45.0` models reasoning ciphertext as optional while compaction ciphertext is required; the recovery path therefore strips only reasoning ciphertext and never mutates compaction.
- #72602 records the live Copilot CAPI matrix: exact original or omitted reasoning IDs are accepted with original ciphertext; synthetic reasoning IDs are rejected.

## Evidence

- Current exact head: `243967371b74bc66113637dbc7ef099e45acaf69`; 8 files, `+729/-241` (970 changed lines, `size: L`).
- Builder-driven Responses continuation proof passed 57 tests, including create-time and streamed rejection, response-ID reset, one shared retry budget, abort/output-start guards, preservation of reasoning/message/function-call/function-output order, unchanged ID-only reasoning, and create/drain compaction no-retry.
- GitHub Copilot connection-bound-ID and stream-wrapper proof passed 15 tests. The focused cold-resume provider integration passed (1 test; 30 unrelated tests skipped).
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint passed for all 8 PR files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Full local tsgo/aggregate lint was blocked by this linked worktree's stale dependency install missing existing `@types/web-push`; no dependency files are changed. Exact-head GitHub CI is running for the current commit.
- The primary cold-resume behavior was previously credentialed-live-tested on the unchanged provider sanitation path: one visible reply, `invalid_encrypted_content = 0`, and `LLM request failed = 0`. The current retry-only follow-up has no local Copilot credential, so that reactive fallback remains an explicit live-proof gap.
- Current-main manual review found no remaining actionable issue after replacing the destructive retry. The prior P1 path that removed reasoning/compaction while retaining tool continuation no longer exists.
- The test-only size compression retained all 57 focused cases; a read-only review found no weakened assertion or shared-state regression.

target.title: fix: provider usage accounting, retry/overflow classification, and output clamping
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider-boundary correctness for Anthropic and Mistral plus shared retry/overflow hardening:

- Anthropic streams crashed with a TypeError when a proxy omitted `usage` from `message_delta` events.
- One-hour prompt-cache writes were billed internally at the five-minute rate (1.25x input) even though the API charges 2x — cost reporting under-counted whenever long cache retention was active. Usage now carries the 1h bucket separately and prices it correctly, keeping the aggregate `cacheWrite` field intact.
- Anthropic-compatible backends that emit and accept empty thinking signatures lost their thinking blocks on replay; an opt-in `allowEmptySignature` compat flag preserves them (default unchanged).
- Mistral prompt caching was never engaged or accounted: requests now send the prompt-cache key and cached-token usage is parsed into `usage.cacheRead`.
- The Anthropic SDK's hidden default retries (2) stacked under the app's own retry policy; the client now defaults to 0 when unset.
- Retry classification missed HTTP 524 (Cloudflare origin timeout), abrupt socket-close failures, and camel-case `ResourceExhausted` — all transient, all previously fatal.
- Context-overflow classification missed parenthesized token-count messages ("maximum context length (262144)") and "maximum allowed input length" phrasings — those errors skipped compaction recovery and stuck sessions.
- Simple-stream requests with a max-token budget near a full context drew provider validation 400s that the overflow classifier cannot recognize; output budgets are now clamped against a conservative input estimate so requests survive and real overflows stay classifiable.

## Why This Change Was Made

These are correctness gaps users hit as crashed streams, silently wrong cost numbers, stuck sessions after context overflow, and hung retries. The classifiers stay purely classificatory; policy remains with the caller.

## User Impact

Anthropic streams tolerate lean proxies; cost reporting is accurate under 1h cache retention; Mistral costs drop via real prompt caching; transient CF/socket/gRPC failures retry instead of failing hard; overflow recovery triggers reliably; near-full-context requests degrade gracefully instead of erroring.

## Evidence

- 163 focused unit tests across 7 files (usage buckets, cost math, compat replay, clamp math, table-driven retry/overflow classifiers).
- **Live verification (real API keys)**: `node scripts/test-live.mjs -- packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.live.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.live.test.ts` — 4/4 passing: Anthropic stream with usage, 1h cache-retention request parsing `cache_creation` buckets with correct cost accounting, thinking-signature survival, and a Mistral stream with cache-field parsing.
- Full changed-file gate green on hosted runner (baselines, three typecheck lanes, lint, boundaries): run 29563721450.
- Plugin-SDK API baseline regenerated via the sanctioned workflow for the additive `Usage.cacheWrite1h` / `allowEmptySignature` contracts; `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` green post-rebase.


**Additional live probes (real API keys):** overflow classification proven against providers' *current* error strings — a deliberately context-exceeding request to Anthropic and to OpenAI Responses each classify as overflow via `isContextOverflow` (guarding compaction recovery against provider error-string drift), and the new output-clamp path completes successfully on a near-full context instead of a validation 400. Anthropic+Mistral 6/6, OpenAI Responses 4/4 keyed runs.

target.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

## Summary

- Complete the existing Control UI MCP App host bridge with safe, text-only `ui/message` support routed through the normal visible chat-send path.
- Advertise messaging only for fresh, authorized app views; reconstructed views remain explicitly read-only.
- Propagate live theme and iframe dimensions through the official MCP Apps host-context bridge without remounting, with observer/listener cleanup on teardown.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI could render MCP App resources and service app tool/resource requests, but an app could not safely ask the user to send plain text through the host chat, and mounted apps did not receive live theme or size changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the already-present iframe/resource reconstruction architecture. It reuses the existing widget-prompt validation and `WIDGET_PROMPT_EVENT` send seam, adds host-owned exact-text confirmation for MCP App requests, and uses the official `AppBridge.setHostContext` lifecycle. It does not add a second send route, config/env surface, protocol version, or privileged approval path.

The implementation adds a small explicit `readOnly` lease marker because a fresh app may legitimately have zero app-callable tools, while a transcript-reconstructed preview must remain resource-only. Tool-count inference could not represent both states safely.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, a visible and focused fresh app can request that the user send one plain-text message. The host shows the exact text for confirmation, then sends through the existing chat composer path. Hidden/background frames, empty or oversized text, slash commands, and rate-limit excesses are rejected. Apps also receive current theme and dimensions as they change.

## Independent landing and backward safety

- The gateway response field is additive. Older Control UIs ignore it; a newer UI talking to an older gateway sees the field absent and installs/advertises no message handler.
- Existing widget prompts use the same extracted validation/send helper without the MCP App confirmation callback; their existing behavior is covered by the widget-prompt and tool-card regression suites.
- App tool/resource handlers, app-only policy, sandbox origins, inner opaque iframe isolation, routes, config, and protocol versions are unchanged.
- Fresh views with an explicit authority set may advertise messaging even when that set is empty. Legacy views without authority and reconstructed `readOnly` views fail closed.
- No behavior enabled by this PR requires a later MCP Apps PR.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: all behavior remains behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Within that gate, `message.text` is advertised only when a fresh view has explicit current-run authority and the host handler is installed. Reconstructed views can still render/read resources but cannot message or call tools. Rich or multi-block `ui/message` content is intentionally unsupported.

## Evidence

- Genuine browser flow: a browser-bundled `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` ran through the real Control UI Vite app, dedicated sandbox HTTP server, and nested iframe bridge. The official initialize handshake advertised `message.text`; exact host consent was required; accepted text produced the normal `chat.send` request (`deliver: false`); the app received its response; live light-theme and container-dimension changes propagated without remounting.
- Focused exact-head proof: 89/89 assertions passed across MCP view leases, transcript reconstruction, gateway authorization, text/focus/visibility/size/rate/slash boundaries, existing widget prompts, host-context updates, and cleanup.
- Production build passed, including the Control UI lazy chunk (`mcp-app-view-registration`, 63.26 kB) and Control UI performance limits.
- Changed-surface checks passed through formatting, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and related policy gates. An earlier Plugin SDK baseline mismatch was independently reproduced on untouched canonical main; the current canonical base includes its unrelated generated/declaration repairs.
- A first CI run exposed a production lint suppression for the SDK's request-style `onmessage` setter. The handler now registers through that documented public setter via a typed wrapper, without a suppression or private schema import; the component and suppression-ratchet tests pass, followed by two clean fresh autoreviews.
- Two fresh autoreviews after the final safety fixes reported no actionable findings (confidence 0.98 and 0.94). Canonical-base updates preserved the exact nine-file product diff.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.node.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.widget-prompts.test.ts`
- Exact-head `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm build`
- Fresh `$autoreview` passes before and after simplification/final safety edits
