target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix(skills): filter NaN from Date.parse in history scan session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resumePendingForBatchScan` in `src/skills/workshop/history-scan.ts` built session cursors by calling `Date.parse(session.updatedAt)` without filtering out `NaN`. When a session's `updatedAt` is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `updatedAtMs` became `NaN`, which then propagated through the resume cursor into subsequent scan iterations.

The downstream comparison `cursor.updatedAtMs > lastReviewedAtMs` returns `false` when `updatedAtMs` is `NaN`, so affected sessions were silently skipped on resume instead of being re-scanned from the correct point.

## Fix

Filter `sessionCursors` so any entry whose `updatedAtMs` is not a finite number is dropped before it can reach the resume cursor. This preserves existing behavior for valid timestamps while ensuring malformed ones cannot poison the resume state.

Export `toStoredState` as a named export (instead of wrapping it in `__testing`) so the knip production deadcode scan does not flag it as unused.

## Evidence

- **Local test run** (3 regression tests pass):

target.title: fix(discord): status probes crash with custom response bodies

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord status probes using a custom fetch adapter could throw an uncaught `TypeError` after a non-OK API response when the response body had no `cancel` method, returned `void` from `cancel`, or threw synchronously during cleanup.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): suppress fallback after route-matched message tool
target.body:
When heartbeat runs in message-tool-only mode, a successful generic message tool delivery can still be followed by duplicate free-text fallback narration in the same Telegram chat.

Fixes #84217

## Affected surface

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`
  - Adds route-matched message tool delivery evidence for heartbeat replies only after the generic message tool sent to the same provider/target/account route.
- `src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds internal reply-payload metadata for route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat-reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds a heartbeat-specific evidence reader.
- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`
  - Suppresses free-text fallback only when the reply carries route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts`
  - Leaves heartbeat payloads available for heartbeat-specific route evidence instead of dropping them via generic message-tool dedupe first.
- Tests:
  - `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.tool-response.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`

## Scope

This is a parameter/evidence threading fix. It does not add a config flag, does not change heartbeat scheduling, and does not touch Slack identity, commitment, or channel-specific private paths.

The important semantic boundary is that "generic message tool delivery evidence" is not the same as "has outbound reply content". This PR only marks heartbeat replies when existing message-tool target evidence matches the same delivery route via the existing `resolveMessagingToolPayloadDedupe` route matcher. Global `messagingToolSentTexts` without route targets is intentionally not enough.

After Vincent's thread-route follow-up, I found one extra current-head issue while refreshing proof: generic reply-payload dedupe could drop the matched heartbeat payload before `heartbeat-runner` saw the route evidence. The current head keeps heartbeat payloads out of that generic dedupe layer so the heartbeat-specific suppression path receives the evidence and can still preserve no-route / wrong-topic fallback behavior.

## Prior art

Prior attempt #84273 was closed by contributor due to inability to provide live channel proof. This PR provides expanded source + runtime helper proof, with the helper semantic explicitly distinguishing "generic message tool delivery evidence" from "has outbound reply content" to address the message-delivery risk flagged in #84273.

The key difference from #84273 is route scope: #84273 marked heartbeat payloads after any message-tool send, while this PR only marks a heartbeat payload when committed `messagingToolSentTargets` match the reply route. If the message tool delivered to another route, or only global text evidence exists, heartbeat fallback still sends.

## Current-head P1 follow-up proof

This update addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Suppress same-route fallback even when the text differs" on head `25958135ed2135dede29e716668ac34cfaea8007`.

The same-route heartbeat evidence rule now treats committed route-matched generic `message` tool target evidence as sufficient for a single plain heartbeat fallback payload, even when the fallback text differs from the tool body. Multi-payload heartbeat replies keep the existing text-match guard so unrelated fallback payloads are not suppressed. Rich payloads, media payloads, reasoning, no-route evidence, wrong-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic evidence remain outside this suppression path.

target.title: feat(feishu): bot-to-bot conversation support with @mention handling
target.body:
## Summary

Makes Feishu bot-to-bot conversations actually work. Bot-authored messages already reach dispatch on `main` (nothing gates them out), so bots could already "talk" — but the experience was broken: replies frequently never reached the peer bot because the `@mention` was missing or used the wrong syntax for the payload, so the conversation silently died. This PR makes bot-to-bot replies reliable — correct, payload-aware `@mention` delivery on every visible path (text, chunked, card, streaming) — and adds opt-in (`allowBots`) plus loop-protection controls. (In a Feishu group a message only notifies the entities it explicitly `@mentions`, so a reply without the right `@` is silently never delivered.)

- Continue treating incoming bot messages like user messages (now gated by an `allowBots` opt-in) so the agent can take part in bot-to-bot threads.
- New `bot-name` resolution module backed by the bot batch API as a weak dependency: falls back to the `open_id` when the bot info scope is absent.
- Per-chat mention registry resolving display name → `open_id` for outbound use.
- Outbound mention handling: teach `<at user_id="...">` syntax in the system prompt, strip only the leading self-mention, preserve + dedup other mentions, escape `<`/`>` in display names.
- Guarantee bot-to-bot replies `@mention` the bot sender via a deterministic `ensureMention` backstop, applied **per outbound unit** (every text chunk and the streaming-card close) using the **syntax that matches the payload** — `<at user_id="...">` for text/post messages, `<at id=...>` for lark_md cards — so the peer bot is notified on every visible path. Replies are delivered inline, not in a topic thread.
- `allowBots` opt-in (default: accept, preserving current behavior) lets operators set `false` to ignore bots or `"mentions"` to accept only when `@mentioned`.
- Shared bot-pair loop guard: bot-authored turns are wired into core `botLoopProtection` (sliding window, on by default) plus a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes.
- Core owns the group reply-delivery mode; the feishu `@mention` hint stays delivery-mode-agnostic (no duplicate delivery-mode computation in the plugin).

Aligns with #71396 — main no longer auto-prepends mentions, so this does not reintroduce the third-party mention cascade: the `mentionTargets` block stays context-only and never tells the model to re-`@` listed users.

Scope: changes are under `extensions/feishu/**` plus the feishu docs page. The one non-plugin file is `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts`, regenerated (`pnpm config:channels:gen`) because the new `allowBots`/`botLoopProtection` config fields must appear in the aggregated bundled-plugin config metadata that the config-metadata check validates.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu` — green, including the new/updated `outbound-mention`, `reply-dispatcher`, `bot` (bot-authored handling), and `monitor` suites covering card vs text mention syntax, per-chunk mentions, `allowBots` gating, and loop-guard suppression.
- `pnpm config:channels:gen --check`, `tsgo`, and `oxlint` clean for the touched surface.
- Real-machine verification in a live Feishu group (see proof below).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a group bot-to-bot reply now `@mentions` the bot sender so the other bot actually receives it — across text messages, chunked replies, and lark_md cards; replies to a human still `@` the human; a silent turn stays `NO_REPLY`. With `allowBots: false` the bot ignores other bots' messages. Previously a bot replying to a bot could omit the `@` (or use the wrong card syntax) and the reply was silently never delivered.

Real environment tested: a live Feishu group containing two bots and one human participant; the agent ran as one bot and replied across multiple turns to the other bot and to the human, under both text and card render modes, and with `allowBots` toggled. (Identifiers below are redacted.)

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran `pnpm config:channels:gen`, rebuilt and restarted the gateway, then drove a multi-turn bot-to-bot exchange in the live group; captured the agent session trajectory and compared it against the messages actually delivered to the group; toggled `allowBots` and a tight `botLoopProtection` window to observe gating.

Evidence after fix:

- On turns where the sender was the other bot, the inbound prompt carried `[System: "<name>" (open_id: ou_<bot-sender-redacted>) is a bot and receives your reply only if you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]`, and the reply led with the bot sender's `<at>` — the peer bot received it.
- `ensureMention` backstop verified live: on a turn where the raw model output omitted the bot sender's `@`, the message actually delivered to the group still contained it — the dispatcher backfilled it.
- Card path verified live: a reply rendered as a lark_md card carried the card mention syntax (`<at id=...>`) and the peer bot received it (the text-form tag would not have notified inside a card).
- `allowBots` verified live: with `allowBots` disabled, the peer bot's messages no longer triggered a reply.

Copied live output from the session (open_ids and names redacted):

```text
# Inbound prompt to the agent — sender is the other bot:
[System: "<bot>" (open_id: ou_REDACTED) is a bot and receives your reply only if
 you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]

# Agent reply that turn, as delivered to the group — leads with the bot sender's <at>:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> 好，背景比较清晰，… (reply continues)

# A later turn whose raw model output dropped the bot-sender @ (it only @'d the
# human). The message ACTUALLY delivered to the group still carried it — the
# dispatcher's ensureMention backfilled the bot sender before sending:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> <at user_id="ou_REDACTED_HUMAN"><human></at> 面试结论：…
```

Observed result after fix: the other bot received and continued the conversation across turns under both text and card modes; no silent drop. `allowBots: false` cleanly suppressed bot-authored replies. Replies addressed exactly the intended target and stayed inline.

What was not tested: the `message_tool` visible-reply path does not receive the deterministic backstop by design (see Design notes); that is an intentional product decision, not an untested gap.

## Design notes

- **Per-payload mention syntax.** Feishu uses two `<at>` forms: `<at user_id="...">Name</at>` for text/post messages and `<at id=...></at>` for lark_md cards. The backstop emits the form matching each outbound unit and re-applies it per chunk and on streaming-card close, so a long or card-rendered bot-to-bot reply notifies the peer on every message.
- **The deterministic backstop is intentionally scoped to the `automatic` reply path, not `message_tool`.** `automatic` is an implicit reply where the agent does not directly control delivery, so the dispatcher guarantees the bot-sender `@`. The `message_tool` path (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`) is an explicit, flexible send where the agent deliberately authors the message, recipients, and mentions; the plugin respects what the agent wrote and does **not** auto-inject — forcing one would override an intentional, author-controlled send. Outbound mention normalization still runs on both paths, so any `@` the agent does write is resolved correctly.
- **Bot-pair loop protection.** Bot-authored messages already reached dispatch on `main` (no gate drops them), so the bot-pair possibility is not introduced here. This PR adds the safety: `allowBots` (default accept; `false`/`"mentions"` to restrict), a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes, and wiring of accepted bot-authored turns into core's shared `botLoopProtection` sliding-window guard (on by default). Tunable/disable-able via `channels.feishu.botLoopProtection`.

target.title: fix: reject unsafe Mattermost API path segments
target.body:
Closes #98389

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost plugin REST calls could reach a different bearer-token endpoint when a dynamic path component contained relative, URL-normalized, or malformed percent-encoded segments.

The affected workflow is Mattermost channel operation through the plugin REST client. Operators expect post, user, and channel ids to select the intended Mattermost endpoint; unsafe path-shaped values should fail before the client attaches the bot token and calls fetch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost client now rejects unsafe API path segments at one shared URL-builder boundary before preparing authorization headers. The direct authenticated media-file download path reuses the same builder. The guard handles raw `.` / `..`, encoded dot segments, backslash separator normalization, URL parser TAB/CR/LF normalization, and malformed percent encoding.

Normal Mattermost paths and request bodies are unchanged. This PR does not alter token storage, account resolution, or Mattermost response handling.

## User Impact

Mattermost users and operators get safer fail-closed behavior for malformed or unexpected REST path inputs. Legitimate Mattermost plugin requests continue to use the same `/api/v4` endpoints.

## Evidence

Before/source proof:

- On current `main`, `buildMattermostApiUrl` appended the requested suffix to `/api/v4` without rejecting dot segments first.
- WHATWG URL parsing normalizes examples like `http://localhost:8065/api/v4/posts/../users/me` to `/api/v4/users/me`, so a path-shaped id can change the endpoint selected under the Mattermost bot token.

After-fix proof on this branch:

target.title: fix(infra): validate callTool arguments against declared inputSchema
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP stdio servers that expose OpenClaw plugin tools (`plugin-tools-serve`, `openclaw-tools-serve`) advertise an `inputSchema` for each tool but do not validate arguments against it before execution. Clients sending malformed arguments get cryptic internal errors rather than clear validation failures, breaking the MCP contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPluginToolsMcpHandlers` in `plugin-tools-handlers.ts` passes `params.arguments ?? {}` directly to `tool.execute()` without checking the tool's parameter schema. The schema is already resolved for `listTools` but is unused in `callTool`.

The fix pre-compiles a TypeBox `Compile` Validator for each tool and calls `validator.Check(args)` before execution. On failure, `[...validator.Errors(args)]` produces structured multi-error messages returned via the MCP `isError` envelope.

This replaces the earlier `validateToolArgs` approach (which only checked `required` + `additionalProperties`) with the canonical full JSON Schema validator from TypeBox 1.3.3, covering type constraints, nested objects, enums, min/max, pattern, and all other JSON Schema keywords.

## User Impact

- MCP clients (Claude Desktop, ACP hosts, IDEs) calling plugin tools with missing required properties now receive a clear `isError: true` response:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "greet": must have required properties name`
- Type mismatches report the path and expected type:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "math_add": a: must be integer; b: must be integer`
- Unexpected properties are rejected when `additionalProperties: false` is declared:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "strict_greet": must not have additional properties`
- No impact on valid tool calls — validation is purely additive and schema-defined
- Existing MCP clients are not affected: `additionalProperties` defaults to `true` per JSON Schema spec, so only tools that explicitly declare constraints are enforced

## Evidence

### Transcript (direct handler invocation — same code path as MCP stdio server)

```
================================================================
  MCP callTool Validation — Live Proof
  PR #109148 — Compile-based full JSON Schema validation
================================================================

Step 1: listTools
  Tool:  greet
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"]}
  Tool:  math_add
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"integer"},"b":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["a","b"]}
  Tool:  strict_greet
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"],"additionalProperties":false}
  Tool:  noop
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{}}

Step 2: VALID arguments
  isError=undefined  content=[{"type":"text","text":"done: greet"}]
  → execute() was called — tool runs normally

Step 3: MISSING required property
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "greet": must have required properties name"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — blocked by validator

Step 4: TYPE MISMATCH
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "math_add": a: must be integer; b: must be integer"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — type constraints enforced

Step 5: UNEXPECTED property (additionalProperties:false)
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "strict_greet": must not have additional properties"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — extra property rejected

Step 6: No-constraint tool
  isError=undefined  content=[{"type":"text","text":"done: noop"}]
  → execute() was called — empty schema accepts anything

Step 7: UNKNOWN tool
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Unknown tool: nonexistent"}]
  → Unknown-tool error (unchanged)

Step 8: EXECUTION error
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool error: internal failure"}]
  → Execution error still reported correctly
```

### Real MCP stdio integration transcript

Proof harness: `StdioClientTransport` (stdin/stdout pipes) → MCP `Server` → `createPluginToolsMcpHandlers`. This exercises the full MCP JSON-RPC protocol through real stdio transport, not just direct handler invocation.

```
================================================================
  MCP callTool Validation — Real MCP Stdio Proof
  PR #109148 — Compile-based full JSON Schema validation
================================================================

Connecting to MCP stdio server...
  → connected

listTools
  Tool:  greet
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"]}
  Tool:  math_add
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"integer"},"b":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["a","b"]}

VALID callTool: greet with { name: "Alice" }
  isError=undefined  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Hello, Alice!"}]
  → execute() was called — tool runs normally

INVALID callTool: greet with {} (missing required 'name')
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "greet": must have required properties name"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — blocked by validator

INVALID callTool: math_add with { a: 'x', b: 'y' } (wrong types)
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "math_add": a: must be integer; b: must be integer"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — type constraints enforced

INVALID callTool: unknown tool name
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Unknown tool: nonexistent"}]
  → Unknown-tool error (unchanged from before fix)
```

### Test results

- `pnpm test src/mcp/`: **115 tests passed** across 14 test files
- `check-test-types`: **passed** — fixed the content union `.text` access by narrowing before reading
- New regression tests (8 cases): missing required properties, type constraints, additionalProperties rejection, valid args pass-through, nested object validation, enum violations, multi-constraint violations, no-constraint tool pass-through
- All existing validation behavior (unknown tool, execution errors) preserved

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(desktop): notifications use native macOS and Windows services

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS and Windows users of the Tauri desktop companion received notifications through the generic desktop backend instead of each platform's modern native notification framework.

## Why This Change Was Made

The desktop companion now uses `tauri-plugin-notifications` from current upstream `main`: Swift `UNUserNotificationCenter` on macOS, Windows notification APIs on Windows, and the existing `notify-rust` desktop backend on Linux. The dependency is pinned to an immutable fork commit because current Swift toolchains need [upstream PR #269](https://github.com/Choochmeque/tauri-plugin-notifications/pull/269) for release linking; the OpenClaw pin can return to upstream after that lands.

Unbundled macOS development binaries skip plugin initialization because Apple's notification framework requires a real app-bundle identity. Signed `.app` bundles retain the normal permission request and notification flow.

## User Impact

macOS and Windows notifications now come from the operating system's native notification service. Linux behavior stays unchanged.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation and dependency behavior.

- Windows Server 2022 / MSVC: native release executable and verified NSIS installer built successfully with Node 24.15.0 and Rust 1.97.1. The exact `tauri-plugin-notifications` Windows backend compiled into the app; installer size 3,751,229 bytes.

target.title: fix(hooks): bound hook workspace manifest and HOOK.md reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace hook discovery read `package.json` and `HOOK.md` through validated file descriptors without bounding the allocated content. A malicious or runaway hook descriptor could therefore exhaust memory during discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both files are small hook metadata. Discovery now reads each already-pinned descriptor through the shared bounded reader with the maintainer-approved 1 MiB limit. This keeps the existing path, symlink, hardlink, and descriptor-identity checks while also bounding files that grow after open.

## User Impact

Oversized hook metadata is warned about and skipped. Discovery continues for other hooks, and an oversized package manifest still falls back to a plain `HOOK.md` in the same directory.

## Maintainer Changes

Related: #109228

## What Problem This Solves

Found by live E2E: interactive Ollama setup exits 1 when any installed model's `/api/show` fails. This was observed with a months-old `gpt-oss:20b` pull returning HTTP 500 on a real machine. One stale model bricks the whole guided path.

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` with canonical agent, workspace-file, and package state
- bind `claws remove` consent to a dry-run `planIntegrity` digest and revalidate the complete plan before mutation
- reuse canonical agent deletion plus existing plugin and skill uninstall lifecycles
- remove only a final, unchanged, Claw-origin package that has not been adopted by a direct install
- retain independently owned, shared, pending, failed, modified, missing, or ambiguous artifacts and report why

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names resolve an install only when unambiguous; final agent ids always work and disambiguate repeated adds.

Remove is a two-step operation. The dry-run records the expected agent identity, managed-file digests, package ownership and canonical state, and root install state in `planIntegrity`. Mutation requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>`, rebuilds the plan, and fails closed if any consent-bearing input changed. Agent drift and unsafe workspace paths block the plan. Missing files are already removed, locally modified files are retained, and unchanged files are moved to nonce staging paths before final validation and deletion.

Package ownership is order-independent. Every Claw reference records whether the package originated from a Claw or existed independently. A later direct plugin or skill install adopts matching references as independently owned. Canonical install timestamps provide a conservative fallback if adoption state cannot be recorded. A final unchanged Claw-origin package is removed only after ownership is re-read immediately before execution, and deletion delegates to the existing plugin or skill uninstall lifecycle. Shared, adopted, drifted, incomplete, or uncertain packages are retained.

If package or file cleanup fails after the agent config commit, the root ledger remains partial and subordinate references stay available for status/doctor recovery. All commands remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and JSON contracts remain experimental.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package installation, ownership, and references
- This PR: lifecycle visibility and consent-bound, ownership-aware cleanup
- Next: #102306 portable export from the same provenance ledger

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across all 17 touched files
- Oxfmt check: all 17 touched files correctly formatted
- 30 focused status/remove/package-adoption tests
- 14 Claws CLI tests
- 158 canonical plugin install tests
- 74 canonical skill install tests
- 7 full lifecycle E2E tests
- `git diff --check`
- Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

`src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` invokes the real `src/entry.ts` CLI in an isolated state directory and passes the complete add -> status -> remove dry-run -> digest-bound consented remove flow. The final result is `openclaw.clawRemoveResult.v1` with `status: "complete"`; canonical agent config is removed and the managed workspace file is deleted.

target.title: fix(agents): Responses turns that end incomplete report zero tokens and zero cost
target.body:
Closes #100954

## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenAI/Azure Responses turn ends with `response.incomplete` — the `max_output_tokens` and
`content_filter` cases, and what Azure emits on early truncation — the agent records **zero tokens and
zero cost** for that turn. The tokens were spent and billed; the session transcript, `usage.cost` RPC and
usage bars just do not see them, so per-session accounting drifts low every time a turn is truncated.

This is the drift reported in #100954.

## Why This Change Was Made

`processResponsesStream` in `src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts` had a terminal branch for
`response.completed` only:

```ts
} else if (type === "response.completed") {
  ...
  if (usage) { output.usage = { ... } }
  calculateCost(model as never, output.usage as never);
  output.stopReason = mapResponsesStopReason(response?.status as string | undefined);
}
```

`response.incomplete` matched no branch in the chain, so the event was silently dropped: `output.usage`
was never written, `output.stopReason` never set. Unlike the package-side processor, this one has no
"stream ended before a terminal response event" guard, so nothing surfaced the miss — the loop just ended
and the turn was reported as free.

**The package side already fixed exactly this.** #109615 finalizes both terminal events through one
`finalizeResponse` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts:963`), which records usage,
cost and service-tier pricing. It did not touch the agent path, and that path is live for the
`openclaw-openai-responses-transport` / `openclaw-azure-openai-responses-transport` runtimes — the Azure
one being #100954's subject. So this is a sibling-parity fix: same bug, same shape of fix, the surface
#109615 left behind.

The recording moves into `src/agents/openai-responses-terminal-outcome.ts` rather than growing
`openai-responses-transport.ts`, which is a legacy file the max-lines ratchet will not let grow. Pulling
the block out drops it from **2502 to 2444 lines**, so the ratchet gets slack instead of pressure.

`reasoningTokens` stays agent-local on purpose: the package-side `Usage` type does not carry it, which is
why the two processors keep separate helpers rather than sharing one.

### Content-filtered turns

Routing `response.incomplete` through the terminal path would otherwise map a content-filtered turn to a
plain `length` stop, while the package side reports it as a provider error
(`openai-responses-shared.ts:991-997`). Rather than leave the two terminal surfaces disagreeing, this
mirrors the package behavior — `stopReason: "error"` with `Provider incomplete_reason: content_filter`.
That is the one behavior here that is not purely additive, and it is pinned by a test.

## Evidence

**The added tests fail on `origin/main` and pass here.** On main the assertions report exactly the
symptom from #100954:

```
× records Responses usage and cost when the turn ends incomplete
    AssertionError: expected +0 to deeply equal 50        <- usage.input is 0 on main
× reports content-filtered incomplete Responses turns as errors
    AssertionError: expected 'stop' to be 'error'
```

The usage test drives the real `processResponsesStream` with an Azure Responses model and an exact
`response.incomplete` event (`max_output_tokens`, populated usage with cached + cache-write tokens), then
asserts the split buckets and priced cost. Sub-cent totals round to zero at `toBeCloseTo`'s default
precision, so it also asserts `toBeGreaterThan(0)`.

**On proof shape:** #109615 pinned the identical package-side behavior with a synthetic terminal event
(`it("finalizes incomplete terminal events with usage")`,
`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts:1281`) rather than a captured provider
transcript. These tests are the same shape against the agent processor.

```
openai-transport-stream*.test.ts + openai-responses*.test.ts   695 passed | 0 failed (18 files)
max-lines ratchet                        OK (openai-responses-transport.ts 2502 -> 2444)
dead-export ratchet (knip)               0 entries
oxlint / oxfmt --check                   clean
tsgo core + test-src                     no errors
```

## Merge Risk

Low. One terminal branch and one extracted helper; no signature, type, config or protocol change. The
`response.completed` path is byte-for-byte the same logic, just relocated — the 695 existing tests across
the transport suites cover it and are unchanged.

The only behavior that moves is the case this fixes: `response.incomplete` now records usage/cost and
sets a stop reason instead of being dropped. Turns that previously reported zero will now report their
real tokens, so per-session totals go **up** for truncated turns — that is the correction, and it is worth
calling out for anyone watching usage dashboards.

This supersedes the agent-side half of #101608, which I opened before #109615 landed the package-side fix;
that PR is now conflicted and half-redundant, so I am closing it in favor of this narrower one.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(sms): prevent silent loss of acknowledged Twilio messages
target.body:
Related: #109657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where incoming Twilio SMS/RCS webhooks could receive a successful TwiML response before OpenClaw had durably admitted the message. Dispatch then ran as detached in-memory work behind a 10-minute/10,000-entry replay guard, so a process failure after the HTTP 200 could silently lose an inbound message; after a 200, Twilio has no failed request to retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SMS plugin now writes the signature-validated raw Twilio form to the shared SQLite channel-ingress queue before returning 200. The durable event id uses Twilio's `MessageSid`, `SmsSid`, or `SmsMessageSid` aliases, sender identity selects the serialized lane, and startup plus interval pumps recover queued work after restart. Parsing and account validation happen at dispatch and permanent invalid payloads are dead-lettered.

The old in-memory replay guard and its saturation 429 path are removed. Completed tombstones retain 24 hours/20,000 entries, strictly covering the retired 10-minute/10,000-key window.

The earlier autoreview P1 claiming ambiguous non-adopted settlement was rejected after tracing the core lifecycle seam: `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` carries adoption, deferral, and abandonment into reply admission; deferred or abandoned work settles through those callbacks, while a normal non-adopted return is terminal local handling. This matches the Telegram reference adapter's `skipped -> completed` mapping.

## User Impact

Acknowledged inbound SMS/RCS messages survive OpenClaw restarts and drain in sender order without replaying completed `MessageSid` events. If durable admission fails, OpenClaw does not acknowledge the webhook. Existing Twilio SID aliases remain accepted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms` — 12 files, 85 tests passed. Coverage includes restart recovery, original receipt timestamps, completed tombstones, handler-reload guard parity, enqueue-before-ack failure, permanent invalid-payload/account dead-lettering, canonical sender lanes, and all Twilio message SID aliases.
- `oxfmt --check <touched SMS files>` — clean.
- `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json <touched SMS files>` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mjs` — production/full-tree/script scans: 0 unused exports.
- `node scripts/check-deadcode-unused-files.mjs` — production/full-tree scans: 0 unused files.

target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets only when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases, so duplicate non-advancing drips fail closed while monotonically advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime. Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only — no new config key or env var. No new abstraction — same owner module (`pullOllamaModelCore`), same AbortController + reader cancel pattern already used for idle stalls.

ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 applied: replaced the prior unconditional one-hour total cutoff with semantic no-progress handling.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeout`, remote Ollama chat streaming (`stream.ts`), or adding a hard total lifetime cap.

**Collision check:** `path:extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` open PRs = 0 for this timeout policy. Nearby open ollama PRs touch streaming/NDJSON elsewhere, not setup pull no-progress.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping `/api/pull` stream (bytes without advancing `completed`) fails closed with a no-progress error instead of hanging the wizard forever. target.title: fix(memory): memory index fails to open when same-file legacy tables diverge
target.body:
Related: #108532
Related: #107220

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators whose per-agent memory database still contains the legacy `meta`/`files`/`chunks` tables would have every Memory Core index open fail with `legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows` once those legacy rows diverge from the canonical `memory_index_*` rows — for example after an upgrade → downgrade → upgrade cycle, where the downgraded build re-creates and re-indexes the legacy tables. The failure repeats on every open (runtime and doctor), and `openclaw doctor --fix` cannot converge it.

#108652 applied the canonical-wins recovery rule to the legacy **sidecar** import in memory-core's doctor contract, but the **same-file** legacy migration in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts` kept the old hard-fail, so this sibling path still wedges — including from inside the sidecar migration itself, where `ensureMemoryIndexSchema` runs outside the conflict-recovery catch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The same-file migration now follows the same rule the sidecar import adopted in #108652: every copied table is derived search state, so a same-identity value mismatch keeps the canonical row and the migration completes (legacy tables are dropped, normal sync rebuilds any skipped rows). The merge is coherent per source: a `(path, source)` the canonical index already tracks keeps **both** its row and its whole chunk set — legacy chunk ids are never imported under a canonical-owned source, so stale legacy text cannot ride into a file that sync considers current (this addresses the review finding on mixed-source coherence). Legacy chunks migrate only together with their legacy-only sources. A legacy row that could not be placed at all by identity (e.g. STRICT rejected it) still aborts and leaves the legacy tables in place, so legacy rows are never silently dropped. Non-goal: the sidecar import path is untouched — it already recovers atomically.

## User Impact

Operators with diverged same-file legacy memory tables get a working memory index and a clean one-time migration on the next start, instead of a permanently failing index open that requires manual SQLite surgery. Canonical index rows and their chunk sets are preserved intact; legacy-only files still migrate with their chunks. Repeated opens are idempotent.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (real on-disk database, before/after)

Method: a driver script (kept outside the repo per the proof-asset rule) exercises the real production `ensureMemoryIndexSchema` from `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts` against a real SQLite file on disk (`node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync`, Node 25.9, via tsx). Nothing is mocked. The database is shaped like the operator upgrade → downgrade → upgrade cycle: a new build creates the canonical index and indexes content (`vectorDims: 1024`, `MEMORY.md` at `new-hash` with canonical chunk `chunk-1` "current canonical body"), then a downgraded build re-creates legacy `meta`/`files`/`chunks` in the same file with diverged values at the same identities (`vectorDims: 512`, `old-hash`, "stale legacy body") **plus a distinct stale legacy chunk id under the canonical-owned file (`chunk-old-7`, "stale legacy tail body")**, plus rows the canonical index does not have (`legacy-only-key`, `old-note.md` with its chunk `chunk-old-2`). The only variable between runs is the `memory-schema.ts` blob (`git hash-object`: `a79b2e4a3835` = origin/main, `df34397c1e41` = this PR).

**BEFORE — origin/main blob `a79b2e4a3835`:** wedged on every open, exactly the released failure from #108532:

```text
=== BEFORE (origin/main memory-schema.ts) ===
open attempt 1: FAILED -> legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
open attempt 2: FAILED -> legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
```

**AFTER — this PR, blob `df34397c1e41` (head `880730ae8c`):** first open migrates and recovers; canonical values win; the stale legacy chunk id under the canonical-owned file is **not** imported; legacy-only rows import with their source; legacy tables drop once; second open is idempotent with identical state:

```text
=== AFTER (with coherence repair) ===
open attempt 1: OK
  legacy tables present: (none)
  memory_index_meta: [{"key":"legacy-only-key","value":"legacy-only-value"},{"key":"memory_index_meta_v1","value":"{\"vectorDims\":1024}"}]
  memory_index_sources: [{"path":"MEMORY.md","hash":"new-hash","size":42},{"path":"old-note.md","hash":"old-note-hash","size":10}]
  memory_index_chunks: [{"id":"chunk-1","text":"current canonical body"},{"id":"chunk-old-2","text":"note body"}]
open attempt 2: OK
  legacy tables present: (none)
  memory_index_meta: [{"key":"legacy-only-key","value":"legacy-only-value"},{"key":"memory_index_meta_v1","value":"{\"vectorDims\":1024}"}]
  memory_index_sources: [{"path":"MEMORY.md","hash":"new-hash","size":42},{"path":"old-note.md","hash":"old-note-hash","size":10}]
  memory_index_chunks: [{"id":"chunk-1","text":"current canonical body"},{"id":"chunk-old-2","text":"note body"}]
```

**Structural-failure retention (both versions):** a legacy `files` row with a `NULL` hash (uncopyable into the STRICT canonical table) still aborts and keeps the legacy tables in place, so legacy rows are never silently dropped:

```text
structural scenario: aborted -> legacy memory files rows could not be copied into canonical memory index rows
  legacy tables retained: chunks, files, meta
  legacy files row retained: [{"path":"broken.md","hash":null}]
```

### Focused tests and lanes

- Regression test "keeps one coherent canonical index when legacy rows diverge" covers the review's mixed-source scenario: conflicting file identity (`doc.md` diverged hash) **with a distinct stale legacy chunk id (`chunk-old-7`)** — asserts the canonical chunk set stays intact, the stale legacy chunk is not imported, the legacy-only source imports with its chunk, and the legacy tables drop. On unpatched `main` this scenario fails with the exact production error string from #108532.
- Negative test "keeps legacy tables when legacy rows cannot be copied" locks the structural-failure abort (savepoint rollback retains legacy tables).
- `pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts` → 24/24 passed (re-run after each rebase).
- `pnpm test src/state/openclaw-database-maintenance.test.ts` → 12/12 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` → clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `pnpm format:check` on the two touched files → clean.
- `extensions/memory-core/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` fails identically on my machine on **clean main** (34× Windows `EBUSY: resource busy` during SQLite temp-dir cleanup), so that suite is environment-blocked locally, not affected by this change; `pnpm check:changed` delegates to Blacksmith Testbox, which is not available to an external contributor — CI on this PR is the authoritative run for those lanes.
- CI note: `build-artifacts` → "Check CLI startup memory" fails on the `status --json` RSS ceiling across runs of this PR on different `main` merge-bases (427.6, 429.4, 427.8 MB vs the 425 MB limit), and unrelated open PRs currently fail the identical step with the same overage (e.g. #109890 at 428.4 MB) while others pass at the same time — the metric is sitting at the ceiling on current `main` merge commits and runner variance decides the outcome. This diff removes production lines in an existing migration function and adds no imports, so it cannot move startup RSS. Per CONTRIBUTING I am not attempting to fix or tune this known `main`-side gate in this PR. (Earlier `check-lint` failures were transient unformatted files landed on `main` — `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`, then `src/infra/spawn-ps.ts` — each fixed on `main` shortly after; cleared by rebasing onto the fixes. Current head `880730ae8c` on latest `main`, source blob `df34397c1e41`.)

AI-assisted: yes — authored with an AI coding agent (Claude); I reviewed the migration ownership boundary, the #108652 sibling semantics, SQLite `INSERT OR IGNORE`/STRICT behavior, and all touched tests. The `autoreview` skill was not available in my environment.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): resolve abortPromise when stop signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a WhatsApp account during or immediately after connection startup would leave `WhatsAppConnectionController.waitForClose()` pending forever when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that race and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The controller built `abortPromise` with an `abort` listener but, when the signal was already aborted at construction time, only called `stopDisconnectRetries()` and never settled `abortPromise`. `waitForClose()` races on that promise, so a pre-aborted stop signal could hang indefinitely. The fix resolves `abortPromise` immediately when `abortSignal.aborted` is already true, matching the existing pre-aborted handling for disconnect retries. Risk note: proof uses the exported controller with a synthetic open connection; live WhatsApp/Baileys sessions were not used.

## User Impact

WhatsApp channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown is requested with an already-aborted stop signal (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

**Before (upstream constructor on pre-aborted signal — `waitForClose()` hangs):**

```
$ git stash push -m proof-before -- extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.ts
$ WA_LABEL=before-fix node --import tsx /tmp/whatsapp-abort-proof.mjs
Worktree: /srv/projects/openclaw-wt-whatsapp-abort-startup
{
  "label": "before-fix",
  "elapsedMs": 501,
  "resolved": false,
  "value": "timeout"
}
$ echo $?
1
```

**After (same harness with fix applied — resolves immediately):**

```
$ WA_LABEL=after-fix node --import tsx /tmp/whatsapp-abort-proof.mjs
Worktree: /srv/projects/openclaw-wt-whatsapp-abort-startup
{
  "label": "after-fix",
  "elapsedMs": 0,
  "resolved": true,
  "value": "aborted"
}
$ echo $?
0
```

The harness drives the exported `WhatsAppConnectionController` with a pre-aborted `AbortController`, injects an open connection whose close promise never settles, and races `waitForClose()` against a 500ms timeout.

Fixes an issue where users running Codex through the app-server integration could see an optional input question keep the turn waiting for a human answer or a broader run timeout, even when Codex supplied an automatic-resolution window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The user-input bridge now preserves the optional app-server deadline, returns an empty answer set when that exact window expires, and clears the timer through the existing request cleanup path after a human answer, abort, replacement request, or server-side resolution.

The implementation follows the current upstream Codex contract at `openai/codex@315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304`: [`autoResolutionMs` is the optional client auto-resolution window](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs#L71-L77), [Codex bounds it before dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs#L123-L133), and [app-server forwards the value to its client](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L703-L746). [The TUI's fixed countdown is an explicitly client-specific policy](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/request_user_input/mod.rs#L281-L300), so OpenClaw honors the app-server wire value instead of copying that policy.

## User Impact

Optional Codex questions can now release the waiting turn automatically at the requested deadline. Human answers still win when submitted in time, and completed or replaced requests leave no stale timer that can affect a later question.

## Evidence

- Focused Node 24.15 proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/user-input-bridge.test.ts` — 1 file and 16 tests passed.
- Fake-timer coverage verifies exact expiry, human-answer cleanup with no second settlement, abort cleanup, and replacement-request timer isolation.
- `oxfmt --check` passed for both changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex adversarial review: no accepted or actionable findings after checking callers, cleanup races, and the upstream protocol contract.

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two catalog rollback guards compared timestamps returned by `Date.parse` without checking for `NaN`:

1. `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts`
2. `isMonotonicRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-snapshot-store.ts`

Both used `Date.parse(candidate.generatedAt) < Date.parse(current.generatedAt)`. When either `generatedAt` string is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `Date.parse` returns `NaN`, and `NaN < NaN` evaluates to `false`. The rollback guards therefore reported "not a rollback" and accepted a candidate that should have been rejected, allowing the catalog snapshot store to move backward to an older or malformed snapshot.

## Fix

Mirror the same defensive policy in both guards:
- If the **candidate's** `generatedAt` is invalid (`NaN`), conservatively treat it as a rollback so malformed candidates cannot downgrade the store.
- If the **current** snapshot's `generatedAt` is invalid, treat the candidate as newer (not a rollback) so a broken current state can still be repaired.

Export `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` and `isMonotonicRollback` as named exports (instead of wrapping in `__testing`) so the knip production deadcode scan does not flag them as unused. Both functions are already called from production code.

## Evidence

- **Local test run** (10 regression tests pass):

target.title: fix: compaction usage guards and agent-loop turn correctness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a cluster of agent-loop and compaction correctness bugs:

- A stream that dies before its terminal usage event persists all-zero usage; that anchors the context-size estimate near zero, threshold auto-compaction silently stops firing, and later requests die on context overflow.
- Tool results without `content` inject `undefined` into the transcript and crash provider conversion on the next request, aborting the run with a malformed message persisted.
- Compaction budgets skipped context-visible entries (plugin-injected messages, branch summaries), so the keep-recent window was computed against the wrong token totals and cut points could not land on those boundaries.
- Compaction could produce empty summary entries when there was nothing to summarize.
- A *successful* response with high token usage could be misclassified as silent overflow, popping the completed assistant message and burning the one-shot overflow-recovery flag.
- A threshold compaction that ran just before delivering a queued user prompt resumed the loop first, so the model answered the compaction summary unprompted.
- Follow-ups queued by handlers reacting to the run ending were never delivered.
- Mid-run system-prompt/tool/model changes did not apply to the next turn on the session path (the wrapper dropped the loop's per-turn refresh context). This is now an explicit `AgentOptions.prepareNextTurnWithContext` API (additive; baseline regenerated via the sanctioned workflow).
- `dispose()` left retry/compaction/branch-summary/bash/agent work running.
- Settings reload did not resync steering/follow-up queue modes; after-tool-call overrides dropped unknown result fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

These bugs compound in long sessions: broken usage accounting disables compaction exactly when it is most needed, and the loop-state gaps surface as duplicated or lost messages. The cut-point/turn-boundary logic is now expressed through one projection helper instead of parallel entry-type switches.

## User Impact

Long sessions keep compacting reliably; runs no longer crash on content-less tool results; queued messages are neither answered out of order nor dropped; mid-run model/prompt/tool changes take effect on the next turn; disposal is clean.

## Evidence

- 56 focused tests passing across `packages/agent-core` (agent-loop, compaction) and `src/agents/sessions` (context-usage, new loop-correctness suite with 10 cases), re-run after rebase onto current `main`.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` and `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (350 entrypoints; additive API only).
- Core + core-test typechecks and changed-file lint green (hosted run 29558685534).


**Live verification (real API keys):** `node scripts/test-live.mjs -- src/agents/sessions/agent-session.live.test.ts` — 3/3 against a real Claude model: a full agent turn with a registered tool executing end-to-end, **manual compaction of a small real session** (this PR's zero-retention replan producing a real model-generated summary, with the session remaining usable), and queued follow-up drain delivering a second answered message. Live suite added in this PR (gated on `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1` + key).

target.title: fix(qqbot): resolve start() when abort signal already fired

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping the QQBot gateway during or immediately after startup would leave `GatewayConnection.start()` pending forever when the caller's `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that promise and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`start()` registered an `abort` listener after `connect()` without checking whether the signal had already fired; per the AbortSignal spec, listeners added to an already-aborted signal never run, so the returned promise never settled. The fix mirrors `waitForDeferredAccountStart` in `src/gateway/server-channels.ts` by returning immediately when `abortSignal.aborted` is already true. target.title: fix(logging): warn when configured file writes fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators using a configured log file could lose file logs without a diagnostic when appends failed. Blank persisted `logging.file` values were also accepted as canonical config even though they cannot identify a usable log file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The logger reports the first failed append in each uninterrupted failure episode and retries later writes without flooding stderr. A successful append clears the warning latch; successful rotation does not, because rotation alone does not prove that writes recovered.

Blank values are repaired at the configuration owner boundary rather than by a runtime fallback: canonical validation rejects empty or whitespace-only `logging.file`, and `openclaw doctor --fix` removes an existing blank field while preserving sibling logging settings. Nonblank paths are not trimmed or otherwise transformed.

## User Impact

Operators receive a concise stderr warning when the configured file cannot be written. Logging recovers on a later successful append without restart, and a later independent failure is reported again.

This is an intentional upgrade contract: configurations with `logging.file: ""` or whitespace now require `openclaw doctor --fix`, which removes that field and restores the default log path. The public logging guide documents this repair path.

## Evidence

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`.
