target.title: fix(line): gateway shutdown hangs when the state store keeps failing during webhook claim writes
target.body:
Closes #109897

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway shutdown hangs forever when the shared SQLite state store keeps failing while a LINE webhook delivery is persisting its claim transition. The spool retries the failed write in an unbounded loop, `stop()` waits on the in-flight delivery, and operators end up hard-killing the process during a store failure, exactly when an unclean kill is most dangerous.

## Why This Change Was Made

The claim-write loop diverged from the bounds the core ingress drain already ships in `commitClaimWriteWithRetry` (`src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts`): a write-attempt cap of 8, an abortable backoff sleep, and a "holding claim" give-up that leaves the row for lease recovery. This change applies the same three bounds to the LINE spool's `persistClaimTransition`. Copying the core drain's stop semantics verbatim (abandon remaining retries as soon as stop is signalled) was considered and rejected: the spool's existing tests pin that a delivered turn's completion persist keeps retrying through `stop()` so a brief store blip cannot become a redelivered duplicate - therefore shutdown cuts only the backoff sleeps, never the bounded write attempts. Migrating LINE onto the core ingress drain wholesale remains a larger architectural move for maintainers to schedule. The unused `abortSignal` parameter on the transition helper (no call site passed it) is removed.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown now completes even while the state store is failing: worst case is the 8 bounded write attempts (~45s when every attempt burns the full SQLite busy timeout) instead of hanging until the store heals or the process is killed. No messages are lost at the new give-up point: the claim is held, stale-claim lease recovery re-delivers the event once the store recovers. Behavior under a transient single failure is unchanged - the completion still persists through shutdown, exactly as the existing regression tests require.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: a persistently failing claim write keeps `stop()` pending indefinitely; bounded semantics should give up, hold the claim, and let shutdown finish.

Real environment tested: real SQLite ingress queue (`createChannelIngressQueueForTests`) driven through the exported `createLineWebhookSpool` factory, with a genuine write lock (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` from a second `node:sqlite` connection) producing real `database is locked` failures; Windows 11, Node 24.15.0.

Before evidence (current main; each attempt blocks on the ~5s busy timeout, then backs off and retries forever):

```
[t+0.1s]   stop() called (gateway shutdown)
[t+5.6s]   completion persist failed; retrying: database is locked   (attempt 1)
[t+11.4s]  attempt 2 ... [t+17.5s] attempt 3 ... [t+146.7s] attempt 16
[t+150.1s] VERDICT: stop() still pending after 150s of persistent SQLITE_BUSY
[t+151.7s] stop() resolved only after the external lock was released
```

Evidence after fix (same harness, same real lock, only the persistence loop changed):

```
[t+0.1s]   stop() called (gateway shutdown)
[t+5.6s]   ... attempts 1-7, backoff sleeps cut by shutdown ...
[t+44.4s]  completion persist failed after 8 attempts; holding claim for lease recovery: database is locked
[t+44.4s]  stop() resolved after 44.3s          <- store still failing
[t+44.4s]  claim held for lease recovery: yes
[t+44.4s]  (lock released) recovery spool re-delivered the event -> {"kind":"completed"}
[t+44.9s]  VERDICT: event recovered and completed after the store healed (no loss)
```

Observed result after fix: shutdown is bounded, the claim survives for lease recovery, and the event completes exactly once after the store heals.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-spool.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  17 passed (17)
```

Control-red: with the source change reverted, the new test "bounds terminal-persistence retries so shutdown cannot hang on a failing store" fails by hanging until the 120s test timeout - the bug demonstrates itself - while the existing single-failure shutdown test still passes, so the suite pins both halves of the semantics.

Additional review: extension source typecheck (`tsconfig.extensions.json`), extension test-types typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`), `pnpm lint:extensions`, and `oxfmt --check` on touched files all pass; the branch is rebased onto current main and the focused suite re-ran green on the rebased head.

What was not tested: no live LINE-platform run - this is process-shutdown behavior whose platform interaction ends at the 200 acknowledgement; the repro drives the exported factory against the real SQLite store with genuine lock contention instead.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: Windows 11 local runs; timeline timestamps vary with the store's busy-timeout scheduling (±0.5s).

target.title: perf(ci): correct pack hints from measured stripe walls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

First measured feedback loop after #109769: the compact PR plan's packing tail dropped 419s -> 299s, but the new tail bin (`compact-small-11`) was overfilled because `core-unit-fast-isolated` actually costs **78.6s on a 4 vCPU runner** against a 25s hint — fork-per-file isolation parallelizes poorly on the small class. Unit-fast stripes also measured far cheaper than hinted (~25-37s vs 100/60) and tooling stripes measured 71-87s.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hint drift directly sets PR wall time now that packing is cost-aware; these are the first corrections from real post-landing group walls (parsed from `[shard:*]` timestamps in compact run 29564411446).

## User Impact

Compact PR bins repack closer to the 220s target: the isolated shard moves to the 8 vCPU class (measured ~50s there), and honest stripe hints stop the packer from overfilling small bins. Expected compact tail: ~250s -> ~230s and better balance; no coverage or topology changes.

## Evidence

- Group walls measured from compact run 29564411446: `core-unit-fast-isolated` 78.6s (4 vCPU), `core-unit-fast-2` 36.7s, `core-tooling-1..4` 87/80/82/71s, `core-tooling-isolated` 44.6s.
- `core-unit-fast-isolated` joins `KEEP_LARGE_NODE_TEST_RUNNER`; verified both plans now route it to `blacksmith-8vcpu` (full-plan shard runner and compact bin class).
- Planner suite green: ci-node-test-plan, ci-changed-node-test-plan, ci-workflow-guards, ci-run-node-test-shard (126 passed, 1 skipped). The compact test now only requires stripe presence — with honest hints, cheap stripes legally co-locate in one bin.
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): clean.

target.title: fix(infra): validate callTool arguments against declared inputSchema
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP stdio servers that expose OpenClaw plugin tools (`plugin-tools-serve`, `openclaw-tools-serve`) advertise an `inputSchema` for each tool but do not validate arguments against it before execution. Clients sending malformed arguments get cryptic internal errors rather than clear validation failures, breaking the MCP contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPluginToolsMcpHandlers` in `plugin-tools-handlers.ts` passes `params.arguments ?? {}` directly to `tool.execute()` without checking the tool's parameter schema. The schema is already resolved for `listTools` but is unused in `callTool`.

The fix pre-compiles a TypeBox `Compile` Validator for each tool and calls `validator.Check(args)` before execution. On failure, `[...validator.Errors(args)]` produces structured multi-error messages returned via the MCP `isError` envelope.

This replaces the earlier `validateToolArgs` approach (which only checked `required` + `additionalProperties`) with the canonical full JSON Schema validator from TypeBox 1.3.3, covering type constraints, nested objects, enums, min/max, pattern, and all other JSON Schema keywords.

## User Impact

- MCP clients (Claude Desktop, ACP hosts, IDEs) calling plugin tools with missing required properties now receive a clear `isError: true` response:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "greet": must have required properties name`
- Type mismatches report the path and expected type:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "math_add": a: must be integer; b: must be integer`
- Unexpected properties are rejected when `additionalProperties: false` is declared:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "strict_greet": must not have additional properties`
- No impact on valid tool calls — validation is purely additive and schema-defined
- Existing MCP clients are not affected: `additionalProperties` defaults to `true` per JSON Schema spec, so only tools that explicitly declare constraints are enforced

## Evidence

### Transcript (direct handler invocation — same code path as MCP stdio server)

```
================================================================
  MCP callTool Validation — Live Proof
  PR #109148 — Compile-based full JSON Schema validation
================================================================

Step 1: listTools
  Tool:  greet
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"]}
  Tool:  math_add
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"integer"},"b":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["a","b"]}
  Tool:  strict_greet
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"],"additionalProperties":false}
  Tool:  noop
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{}}

Step 2: VALID arguments
  isError=undefined  content=[{"type":"text","text":"done: greet"}]
  → execute() was called — tool runs normally

Step 3: MISSING required property
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "greet": must have required properties name"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — blocked by validator

Step 4: TYPE MISMATCH
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "math_add": a: must be integer; b: must be integer"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — type constraints enforced

Step 5: UNEXPECTED property (additionalProperties:false)
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "strict_greet": must not have additional properties"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — extra property rejected

Step 6: No-constraint tool
  isError=undefined  content=[{"type":"text","text":"done: noop"}]
  → execute() was called — empty schema accepts anything

Step 7: UNKNOWN tool
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Unknown tool: nonexistent"}]
  → Unknown-tool error (unchanged)

Step 8: EXECUTION error
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool error: internal failure"}]
  → Execution error still reported correctly
```

### Real MCP stdio integration transcript

Proof harness: `StdioClientTransport` (stdin/stdout pipes) → MCP `Server` → `createPluginToolsMcpHandlers`. This exercises the full MCP JSON-RPC protocol through real stdio transport, not just direct handler invocation.

```
================================================================
  MCP callTool Validation — Real MCP Stdio Proof
  PR #109148 — Compile-based full JSON Schema validation
================================================================

Connecting to MCP stdio server...
  → connected

listTools
  Tool:  greet
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"]}
  Tool:  math_add
  inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"integer"},"b":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["a","b"]}

VALID callTool: greet with { name: "Alice" }
  isError=undefined  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Hello, Alice!"}]
  → execute() was called — tool runs normally

INVALID callTool: greet with {} (missing required 'name')
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "greet": must have required properties name"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — blocked by validator

INVALID callTool: math_add with { a: 'x', b: 'y' } (wrong types)
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Invalid arguments for tool "math_add": a: must be integer; b: must be integer"}]
  → execute() was NOT called — type constraints enforced

INVALID callTool: unknown tool name
  isError=true  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Unknown tool: nonexistent"}]
  → Unknown-tool error (unchanged from before fix)
```

### Test results

- `pnpm test src/mcp/`: **115 tests passed** across 14 test files
- `check-test-types`: **passed** — fixed the content union `.text` access by narrowing before reading
- New regression tests (8 cases): missing required properties, type constraints, additionalProperties rejection, valid args pass-through, nested object validation, enum violations, multi-constraint violations, no-constraint tool pass-through
- All existing validation behavior (unknown tool, execution errors) preserved

target.title: fix(ci): bound openclaw-npm-release git fetch operations with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `openclaw-npm-release` workflow could remain stuck in any of four `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks the npm release pipeline and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

All four `git fetch` commands now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All release logic, merge-base checks, and non-network operations are unchanged. The four locations are: alpha preflight (line 125), tagged release (line 266), main fetch (line 733), and alpha publish (line 894).

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing an npm release runner for the full job timeout before the release begins.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts --run --testNamePattern="bounds openclaw-npm-release git fetch"` ??1 passed.

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each of the four production workflow steps, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a Git transport that stalls until `TERM`. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds, the Git fixture observed `TERM`, and none reached the five-second outer watchdog. The identical pattern was proven for all five Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete test suite was also attempted: 72 tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases failed because the isolated host lacked GitHub CLI authentication/clean login-shell state. The affected focused regression is green.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

Cyber:

```text
Config valid: /home/umbrel/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Gateway ready after restart
Health: Discord configured, Telegram configured, WhatsApp linked
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/embedded-agent-Cv8lGIPa.js: createEmbeddedHookSessionResetQueue present
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

Sovereign:

```text
Telegram: configured
Gateway event loop: ok

/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

Post-restart log probes on both hosts showed no new `api.resetSession not available` messages in the verification window.

## Validation

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` was present but contained only whitespace. The AWS SDK accepts whitespace values in both its static environment credential provider and its Bedrock bearer-token environment provider, preventing fallback to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicitly configured bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication. A shared credential-preparation path removes only whitespace bearer/static/session environment values before shared-config refresh and credential resolution; streaming, discovery, embeddings, and control-plane profile resolution all pass through that path. The same sanitization now also runs before the bundled Mantle plugin generates IAM bearer tokens via `@aws/bedrock-token-generator`, covering the last remaining Bedrock auth path that invokes the AWS SDK default credential chain. Valid static credentials remain unchanged.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider checks static values for truthiness rather than trimmed content, while `fromEnvSigningName({ signingName: "bedrock" })` accepts any present `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` value. Removing blank values lets the SDK continue through its normal default chain.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials across streaming, model discovery, embeddings, and inference-profile resolution. Valid bearer tokens and static credentials remain supported; explicitly configured bearer tokens are normalized before use.

## Evidence

- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- Real AWS SDK default-chain proof used an isolated temporary `[default]` shared credentials file, with no network call or real credentials. Before preparation, the SDK selected both whitespace static env credentials and a whitespace Bedrock bearer env token. After preparation it removed those blank values, rejected the missing bearer env token, and resolved the temporary default profile. Redacted result: `{"beforeSelectedWhitespaceStaticEnv":true,"beforeSelectedWhitespaceBearerEnv":true,"blankEnvRemoved":true,"afterSelectedDefaultProfile":true,"blankBearerRejected":true}`.
- Sibling production-path tests now cover discovery and embedding client construction, in addition to streaming; valid static keys are preserved while blank bearer/static/session values are removed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` — 4 files, 97 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts` — mantle credential sanitization tests pass; full mantle suite (3 files, 54 tests) and full bedrock suite (10 files, 175 tests) also pass.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files.
- `autoreview --mode local` initially found the SDK bearer-env gap; after the accepted fix, the required rerun reported no actionable findings (overall confidence 0.97).

I reviewed the streaming, discovery, embedding, provider-registration, and inference-profile control-plane paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@3.972.61`, and `@aws-sdk/token-providers` contracts.

target.title: feat(bedrock): enable prompt caching for Nova models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #29707. Amazon Nova generation models on Bedrock were still treated as unsupported non-Anthropic models, so OpenClaw forced `cacheRetention: "none"` and never emitted Bedrock `cachePoint` blocks for Nova requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

AWS documents explicit prompt caching support for Amazon Bedrock models, including Nova generation models: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html

This change teaches the Bedrock provider to recognize Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, Premier, and Nova 2 Lite refs, lets direct Nova requests keep their explicit cache settings, and keeps the existing no-cache fallback for unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models. For Nova, `cacheRetention: "long"` emits the default Bedrock cache point without reusing Claude's `ttl: "1h"` field.

Nova eligibility now has a single owner: the Amazon Bedrock provider normalization seam. The provider sets generic runtime compatibility metadata for eligible Nova models, while the shared agent cache-retention path only consumes that capability and contains no Bedrock model IDs or Nova-family matcher.

## User Impact

Users can enable prompt caching for Bedrock Nova text models without hitting the previous runtime no-cache override. Unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models, such as Mistral, continue to be protected from unsupported cache metadata.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale encrypted reasoning failures
target.body:
fix #95441

Related: #95493
Related: #95587

AI-assisted: yes (GitHub Copilot).

## What Problem This Solves

Persisted GitHub Copilot reasoning can become invalid when OpenClaw reconstructs a session, causing `invalid_encrypted_content` or a missing reply on a later turn. The rejection can happen while creating a Responses request or after its SSE stream opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses the existing owner boundaries:

- **Cold replay history:** the GitHub Copilot provider's `sanitizeReplayHistory` hook removes persisted thinking/reasoning when a Copilot Responses `AgentSession` is rehydrated. The sanitized history becomes that session's in-memory state, while reasoning generated later in the same agent/tool loop remains available.
- **Active wire payload:** the provider boundary preserves complete native `rs_*` reasoning, converts Copilot connection-bound reasoning IDs to idless replay, keeps already-idless reasoning, and removes foreign, malformed, or incomplete reasoning. Existing message/function-call ID normalization remains intact.
- **Single bounded recovery:** Responses request creation and SSE draining share one retry budget. Before any public model output, a recognized encrypted-content failure retries once after removing only the top-level `encrypted_content` field from reasoning items. The retry preserves reasoning summaries and IDs, assistant messages, function calls, function outputs, and their order. Requests containing compaction fail closed instead of dropping compaction or constructing an item without its required ciphertext.

This separates prevention from recovery because neither is sufficient alone. Applying only a broad replay policy would discard valid same-loop continuity; relying only on recovery would keep sending known-stale state and make provider failure part of the normal path. Provider-owned cold sanitation plus one bounded generic fallback avoids both without adding session state, configuration, or a compatibility path.

The change adds no configuration, persisted replay state, transcript mutation, or public SDK surface.

## User Impact

Rehydrated Copilot sessions no longer send persisted opaque reasoning. Valid same-loop reasoning and tool continuation remain available. If a provider rejects stale reasoning before output starts, recovery preserves the continuation structure; compaction remains untouched and fails closed.

## Upstream Behavior References

- [`@github/copilot@1.0.69-2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot/v/1.0.69-2), build `546d22a58d`: active history retains encrypted reasoning, while cold resume, abort/cancel, and effective-model history rewrite strip opaque reasoning.
- [`github/copilot-sdk@5adb51b`](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/5adb51b9e2ac50ad4876e756fa8c05549c1490fd/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts#L1044-L1054) documents OpenAI encrypted reasoning as session-bound and stripped on resume.
- [`microsoft/vscode@47657de`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L145-L172) requests `reasoning.encrypted_content`; its [history selection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L306-L395) excludes pre-marker history, and its [serializer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L631-L660) replays only complete Responses reasoning.
- OpenAI Node `6.45.0` models reasoning ciphertext as optional while compaction ciphertext is required; the recovery path therefore strips only reasoning ciphertext and never mutates compaction.
- #72602 records the live Copilot CAPI matrix: exact original or omitted reasoning IDs are accepted with original ciphertext; synthetic reasoning IDs are rejected.

## Evidence

- Current exact head: `243967371b74bc66113637dbc7ef099e45acaf69`; 8 files, `+729/-241` (970 changed lines, `size: L`).
- Builder-driven Responses continuation proof passed 57 tests, including create-time and streamed rejection, response-ID reset, one shared retry budget, abort/output-start guards, preservation of reasoning/message/function-call/function-output order, unchanged ID-only reasoning, and create/drain compaction no-retry.
- GitHub Copilot connection-bound-ID and stream-wrapper proof passed 15 tests. The focused cold-resume provider integration passed (1 test; 30 unrelated tests skipped).
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint passed for all 8 PR files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Full local tsgo/aggregate lint was blocked by this linked worktree's stale dependency install missing existing `@types/web-push`; no dependency files are changed. Exact-head GitHub CI is running for the current commit.
- The primary cold-resume behavior was previously credentialed-live-tested on the unchanged provider sanitation path: one visible reply, `invalid_encrypted_content = 0`, and `LLM request failed = 0`. The current retry-only follow-up has no local Copilot credential, so that reactive fallback remains an explicit live-proof gap.
- Current-main manual review found no remaining actionable issue after replacing the destructive retry. The prior P1 path that removed reasoning/compaction while retaining tool continuation no longer exists.
- The test-only size compression retained all 57 focused cases; a read-only review found no weakened assertion or shared-state regression.

target.title: fix(ai): preserve Unicode in provider error bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could receive malformed provider error text when an external API response body placed an emoji or another non-BMP character at the truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared provider-error formatter now uses the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper instead of splitting the string at an arbitrary code unit. This keeps the existing 4,000-code-unit cap and output format unchanged while preventing lone surrogates.

## User Impact

Provider failures continue to include a bounded response-body excerpt, but the excerpt is now valid Unicode even when the boundary falls inside an emoji.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression case with 3,999 ASCII code units followed by an emoji, reproducing the exact split boundary.
- Node 24 Docker proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.test.ts` passed 1 file / 5 tests.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview against current `upstream/main` completed with no actionable findings.

### Exact-head built-package boundary proof

- Inspected successful CI run `29564719443` for exact head `c38921555e5234e91ea6a07abd3861120abda0b7`; `build-artifacts` and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed.
- Downloaded `dist-runtime-build` artifact `8400705348`; archive SHA-256 is `9863a46e89b98e2a216a581128774d0f02d59e9719cf583eceb9561842ed0f2b`, and `zstd -t` passed.
- The artifact contains 44 emitted files under `packages/ai/dist`. Searching that entire tree for `@openclaw/normalization-core` returned zero matches.
- `provider-error-CDmoLcmM.mjs` imports `truncateUtf16Safe` through the relative chunk `./transform-messages-Dz5aG0D0.mjs`; that chunk contains the bundled `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` implementation.

This proves the workspace helper is bundled into the emitted `@openclaw/ai` JavaScript and is not an unresolved runtime dependency.

### Packaged provider-adapter runtime proof

- Created an npm tarball from the exact-head CI `packages/ai/dist` output and the exact-head package metadata; tarball SHA-256 is `3f11d7f3db37e7992948547d03a062e300bc0bb1c6ec4a3bf11c1970581c6faa`.
- Installed that tarball with scripts disabled into an empty consumer. The installed dependency tree does not contain `@openclaw/normalization-core`.
- Under Node `v24.18.0`, imported the public `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai` entry and ran `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint.
- The adapter sent `/v1/chat/completions`; the endpoint returned a 502 JSON error whose independently serialized long body placed the emoji's high surrogate at code-unit index 3,999.

Redacted output:

```text
PACKAGED_PROVIDER_PROOF_109786 {"packageEntry":"@openclaw/ai/internal/openai","requestPath":"/v1/chat/completions","serializedErrorBoundary":3999,"stopReason":"error","errorMessageLength":4019,"endsWithTruncationMarker":true,"hasLoneSurrogate":false,"boundarySuffix":"xxxxxxxx... [truncated]"}
```

This is an installed-package and real provider-adapter HTTP-path probe using a local deterministic error endpoint. It does not claim an external provider credential run.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; the behavior, dependency boundary, diff, and test evidence were reviewed before submission.

target.title: fix(coding-agent): isolate Codex CLI CODEX_HOME from OpenClaw OAuth in skill launch forms
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users launching Codex workers from the bundled
`coding-agent` skill could reuse the ambient `~/.codex` ChatGPT OAuth state
that OpenClaw also depends on, which can leave one client failing with
`refresh_token_reused`.

Fixes #109704

## Why This Change Was Made

The manual Codex launch forms now require an authenticated `CODEX_HOME` outside
every Git worktree, and the scratch recipe logs in the isolated home before
running `codex exec`. The credential warning now matches Codex's supported
storage modes instead of implying that OAuth state is always in `auth.json`.

## User Impact

Users can run Codex background workers without placing Codex credentials in a
checkout or accidentally launching scratch workers from an empty auth store.

## Evidence

- Codex source inspection: `CODEX_HOME` selects the Codex home directory, and
  CLI auth may use file, keyring, or auto keyring-with-file-fallback storage
  (`codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs`, `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`,
  `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs`, `codex-rs/login/src/server.rs`).
- Negative control: a fresh empty `CODEX_HOME` reports `Not logged in`, so the
  old scratch shape cannot complete an authenticated turn without login.
- Real scratch path: a temporary Git repo plus an authenticated external
  `CODEX_HOME` completed `codex exec` and returned the requested message.
- `pnpm docs:list`
- `git diff --check 5024c100a3244d605a7f874d3d48c842110f6a5c...HEAD`

```text
$ TMP_CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d); chmod 700 "$TMP_CODEX_HOME"; CODEX_HOME="$TMP_CODEX_HOME" codex login status
Not logged in

$ SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d); git -C "$SCRATCH" init
$ CODEX_HOME=<authenticated-external-home> codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
$ CODEX_HOME=<authenticated-external-home> codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -C <tmp-git-repo> --output-last-message <proof-output> 'Reply exactly: isolated-codex-home-ok'
workdir: <tmp-git-repo>
last_message:
isolated-codex-home-ok
```

AI-assisted: built with Codex

target.title: feat(bedrock): enable prompt caching for Nova models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #29707. Amazon Nova generation models on Bedrock were still treated as unsupported non-Anthropic models, so OpenClaw forced `cacheRetention: "none"` and never emitted Bedrock `cachePoint` blocks for Nova requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

AWS documents explicit prompt caching support for Amazon Bedrock models, including Nova generation models: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html

This change teaches the Bedrock provider to recognize Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, Premier, and Nova 2 Lite refs, lets direct Nova requests keep their explicit cache settings, and keeps the existing no-cache fallback for unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models. For Nova, `cacheRetention: "long"` emits the default Bedrock cache point without reusing Claude's `ttl: "1h"` field.

Nova eligibility now has a single owner: the Amazon Bedrock provider normalization seam. The provider sets generic runtime compatibility metadata for eligible Nova models, while the shared agent cache-retention path only consumes that capability and contains no Bedrock model IDs or Nova-family matcher.

## User Impact

Users can enable prompt caching for Bedrock Nova text models without hitting the previous runtime no-cache override. Unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models, such as Mistral, continue to be protected from unsupported cache metadata.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1` on all 9 follow-up files

target.title: fix(heartbeat): suppress fallback after route-matched message tool
target.body:
When heartbeat runs in message-tool-only mode, a successful generic message tool delivery can still be followed by duplicate free-text fallback narration in the same Telegram chat.

Fixes #84217

## Affected surface

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`
  - Adds route-matched message tool delivery evidence for heartbeat replies only after the generic message tool sent to the same provider/target/account route.
- `src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds internal reply-payload metadata for route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat-reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds a heartbeat-specific evidence reader.
- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`
  - Suppresses free-text fallback only when the reply carries route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts`
  - Leaves heartbeat payloads available for heartbeat-specific route evidence instead of dropping them via generic message-tool dedupe first.
- Tests:
  - `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.tool-response.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`

## Scope

This is a parameter/evidence threading fix. It does not add a config flag, does not change heartbeat scheduling, and does not touch Slack identity, commitment, or channel-specific private paths.

The important semantic boundary is that "generic message tool delivery evidence" is not the same as "has outbound reply content". This PR only marks heartbeat replies when existing message-tool target evidence matches the same delivery route via the existing `resolveMessagingToolPayloadDedupe` route matcher. Global `messagingToolSentTexts` without route targets is intentionally not enough.

After Vincent's thread-route follow-up, I found one extra current-head issue while refreshing proof: generic reply-payload dedupe could drop the matched heartbeat payload before `heartbeat-runner` saw the route evidence. The current head keeps heartbeat payloads out of that generic dedupe layer so the heartbeat-specific suppression path receives the evidence and can still preserve no-route / wrong-topic fallback behavior.

## Prior art

Prior attempt #84273 was closed by contributor due to inability to provide live channel proof. This PR provides expanded source + runtime helper proof, with the helper semantic explicitly distinguishing "generic message tool delivery evidence" from "has outbound reply content" to address the message-delivery risk flagged in #84273.

The key difference from #84273 is route scope: #84273 marked heartbeat payloads after any message-tool send, while this PR only marks a heartbeat payload when committed `messagingToolSentTargets` match the reply route. If the message tool delivered to another route, or only global text evidence exists, heartbeat fallback still sends.

## Current-head P1 follow-up proof

This update addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Suppress same-route fallback even when the text differs" on head `25958135ed2135dede29e716668ac34cfaea8007`.

The same-route heartbeat evidence rule now treats committed route-matched generic `message` tool target evidence as sufficient for a single plain heartbeat fallback payload, even when the fallback text differs from the tool body. Multi-payload heartbeat replies keep the existing text-match guard so unrelated fallback payloads are not suppressed. Rich payloads, media payloads, reasoning, no-route evidence, wrong-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic evidence remain outside this suppression path.

```text
RED before implementation:
AssertionError: expected undefined to be true
```

The earlier Mantis Telegram workflow could not run because this actor lacks write/maintain/admin permission, so I reran the current-head proof locally with the existing Telegram proof credential and a temporary harness outside the patch. The harness used the real current-head route-evidence path:

target.title: fix: generated image delivered twice after image_generate completion
target.body:
Closes #108976

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating an image in a Telegram (or other channel) chat would receive the same photo twice—once from the resumed agent reply that re-attached media, and once from the completion handoff that already owns delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generated-media completion handoffs already own outbound media delivery (durable host-owned media with direct fallback). The success reply instruction previously told the resumed agent to also attach every `MEDIA` path / structured attachment, which creates a second visible delivery of the same artifact when the agent follows that prompt.

The instruction now assigns a single owner: the completion handoff delivers media; the agent may only write a short caption (or `NO_REPLY`). Image, video, and music generation share this lifecycle helper, so the ownership rule applies across those sibling tools without a Telegram-specific branch.

Compatibility: no config, API, or protocol change. Performance: prompt-text only, no extra I/O. Usability: captions remain allowed; images no longer duplicate. Security: no trust-boundary or secret changes.

## User Impact

After `image_generate` (and sibling media generation tools) completes, users receive each generated artifact once, with an optional caption, instead of two identical channel deliveries a few seconds apart.

## Evidence

Focused tests (local macOS):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  35 passed (35)
```

Coverage:

- Shared regression `assigns completion-handoff ownership so the agent is not told to re-attach MEDIA` asserts the wake `replyInstruction` names completion-handoff ownership, forbids re-attaching MEDIA lines, and no longer contains the old dual-attach wording.
- Sibling `music-generate-background` expectations now match that same shared ownership contract (completion handoff owns media; agent is caption-only). This aligns the music completion path with image/video under the shared helper and clears the CI failure that still expected `final-reply MEDIA lines`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: generated media from `image_generate` (and sibling media tools via the shared helper) must be delivered once; completion handoff owns media while the agent may only caption.
- Environment: local macOS OpenClaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: success reply instruction told the resumed agent to attach every generated media path with final-reply MEDIA lines (or message-tool attachments) while `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff` also carries the same mediaUrls/attachments into host-owned delivery.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Inspect `buildMediaGenerationReplyInstruction` for status `ok`.
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts -t "completion-handoff ownership"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts` → 35/35 pass.
- Evidence after fix: ownership regression passes; music sibling expectations assert completion-handoff ownership and forbid MEDIA re-attach; instruction text requires caption-only / NO_REPLY guidance.
- Control check: wake still sets `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff: true` and still includes `mediaUrls` / attachments on the internal event for host delivery evidence; only the agent-facing ownership instruction changed.
- Observed result after fix: completion wake no longer instructs a second media-bearing reply path for image or music (shared helper).
- Live Telegram: still needed for full acceptance (exactly one `sendPhoto` after one image-generation completion, with caption behavior). A prior Mantis Telegram Desktop run on this PR could not capture a faithful generated-media completion sequence (capture infrastructure / skipped before-after; no visual artifacts), so it did not substitute for a successful single-delivery recording. Happy to re-run or supply a redacted recording when a Telegram tenant path is available.

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
@
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Rebase Note

Rebased onto current main (9ddd988c9) to pick up the rename `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout`. The private helper `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` is now re-exported for direct testing.

## What Changed (vs previous revision)

- **Rebased onto main**: Resolved merge conflicts with the `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` rename and added test for stalled DNS preflight.
- **Re-exported `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo`**: The function was un-exported during the main rename; re-exported so bounded-read tests can target it directly.
- **Fixed lint**: Added curly braces to `if (res.destroyed) return;` one-liners in the test (eslint `curly`).

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

**Non-transient overflow:** Size overflow now throws as non-transient (`transient: false`) so the detail message propagates to callers instead of being swallowed by the generic "fetch failed" wrapper.

## Evidence

### 1. Static / focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts --run: 9/9 passed
```

Tests cover: body-less success, body-less oversized rejection, **real loopback HTTP streaming oversized rejection** (pre-read bound verified), mutation test, guarded fetch bounded reads, DNS stall timeout, and existing metadata/timeout regression tests.

### 2. Standalone real-behavior proof (terminal transcript)

A standalone proof harness (`gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts`) exercises the REAL production function with real Node.js loopback HTTP:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts --run --reporter verbose

 RUN  v4.1.9 G:/AI学习/openclaw

stdout | gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts > standalone real-behavior proof > parses under-cap streaming response from a real loopback HTTP server
  [proof] starting real loopback HTTP server (under-cap) ...
  [proof] server listening on 127.0.0.1:62187
  [proof] response status=200 content-length=chunked
  [proof] ✓ parsed: url=wss://gateway.discord.gg/ shards=1
  [proof] ✓ session_start_limit: total=1000 remaining=999 max_concurrency=1
  [proof] server closed

stdout | gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts > standalone real-behavior proof > rejects oversized chunked response at the streaming 4 MiB boundary
  [proof] starting real loopback HTTP server (oversized chunked) ...
  [proof] server listening on 127.0.0.1:62189, streaming 4456448 bytes (4.3 MiB) in 64 KiB chunks
  [proof] fetch resolved, body is streaming (no content-length)
  [proof] calling fetchDiscordGatewayInfo (production fn with streaming pre-read bound) ...
  [proof] ✓ streaming pre-read bound rejected: Failed to get gateway information from Discord: Discord gateway metadata response body too large: 4259797 bytes (limit: 4194304 bytes)
  [proof] server closed

 ✓ standalone real-behavior proof > parses under-cap streaming response from a real loopback HTTP server 205ms
 ✓ standalone real-behavior proof > rejects oversized chunked response at the streaming 4 MiB boundary 73ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What this proves:**
- Real Node.js `http.createServer` streams 4.3 MiB of chunked JSON (64 KiB chunks)
- Real Node.js `fetch` connects to loopback TCP
- Production function `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` receives the real streaming `Response`
- `readResponseWithLimit` reads chunks via `reader.read()` in a bounded loop
- At the 4 MiB boundary: stream is cancelled, `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` throws non-transient error with `transient: false`

target.title: fix(xai): add handshakeTimeout to TTS stream WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI TTS stream creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The existing `connectTimer` fires after `timeoutMs` and calls `failConnect()`, which **rejects the promise but does not close or terminate the WebSocket** — the underlying TCP connection and its memory remain occupied. The `handshakeTimeout` at the ws library level cleans up the TCP connection when the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade stalls.

The voice bridge was excluded: its `connectTimeout` already calls `ws.terminate()`, which the pinned ws library aborts the active request and destroys the socket even in CONNECTING state.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: timeoutMs` (30 s default) — passes the existing timeout parameter to the ws constructor so the library itself enforces the upgrade deadline and releases TCP resources.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS connections now release TCP resources within their configured timeout instead of leaking them until GC. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER (5 s)","handshakeTimeoutMs":5000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":5015}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally).
- **AFTER**: `"Opening handshake has timed out"` at 5015 ms — terminated within deadline.

### Why only TTS (not voice bridge)

| Function | Existing timeout mechanism | Cleans up TCP? | handshakeTimeout needed? |
|------|------|------|------|
| `xaiTTSStream` | `connectTimer → failConnect()` | **No** — only rejects promise | ✅ Yes |
| `XaiRealtimeVoiceBridge` | `connectTimeout → ws.terminate()` | Yes — terminate() destroys socket | ❌ No (reverted) |

### Focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/tts.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  26 passed (26)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  36 passed (36)
```

- `expect(ws?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(5_000)` — timeoutMs reaches ws constructor.

commands.command: openclaw plugins update/install fails with "npm view produced incomplete package metadata" on npm 12 environment openclaw: 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4) node: v26.4.0 npm: 12.0.1 (fails) / 10.9.8 (works) os: cachyos linux, kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos-server-lto (x86_64) registry: reproduced on both registry.npmjs.org and registry.npmmirror.com summary on npm 12, every openclaw plugins update --all and plugin install reports npm view produced incomplete package metadata and the operation fails. downgrading npm to v10 resolves it completely. the failure is not network/registry/package-existence related — all official plugins (discord, slack, email, longcat, wecom, etc.) resolve fine on npm 10 and via direct npm view on npm 12. steps to reproduce have npm 12.x installed (npm --version → 12.x) run openclaw plugins update --all or openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" observed behavior could not check discord before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata could not check email before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... failed to update discord: npm view produced incomplete package metadata failed to update email: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... for a direct install, the package tarball downloads and extracts successfully, but then: downloading @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin… extracting .../tencent-weixin-openclaw-weixin-2.4.6.tgz… npm view produced incomplete package metadata expected behavior plugin metadata check succeeds and the plugin installs / updates normally. root cause (analysis) openclaw's install/update flow calls: npm view <spec> name version dist.integrity dist.shasum openclaw --json --before=<now> and then requires the parsed result to contain name + version (see dist/install-source-utils-*.js, resolvenpmspecmetadata): const metadata = normalizenpmviewmetadata(json.parse(res.stdout.trim())); if (!metadata?.name || !metadata.version) return { ok:false, error:"npm view produced incomplete package metadata" }; on npm 12 the npm view --json output format / field shape differs from what this parser expects, so the guard trips even though the package exists and the tarball downloads fine. on npm 10 the same call returns the expected shape and everything works. evidence direct npm view @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin version on npm 12 → 2.4.6 (package exists, network fine) same npm view ... --json --before=... shape is what openclaw invokes; parse guard fails on npm 12 after npm install -g npm@10:and openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" → installed plugin: openclaw-weixin workaround downgrade npm to v10: npm install -g npm@10 then restart the gateway (systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway.service). suggested fix make resolvenpmspecmetadata tolerant of the npm 12 --json output shape (e.g. handle array vs object, and don't require the openclaw field for the existence/version check), or pin a known-good npm version range for the metadata check.

### Summary

On macOS, upgrading an existing npm/Homebrew-style OpenClaw install to `2026.7.1` can leave external plugins in a split-brain state:

1. a legacy plugin install metadata conflict prevents startup migrations from completing, so the gateway refuses readiness
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` does **not** clear it
3. after manual uninstall/reinstall of the conflicting plugin, the gateway can recover, but other external plugins may still have stale install/index state
4. during follow-up repair, a working plugin can silently lose its config entry / allowlist entry / API-key subtree, so the plugin is physically installed and partially loaded, but the capability is unusable until config is manually restored
5. even after successful recovery and a real successful capability call, some status surfaces still report old version drift

This leaves the system operational only after manual intervention across multiple layers (`plugins.entries.*`, `plugins.allow`, plugin reinstall, gateway restart), and the built-in repair flow does not converge state automatically.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a long-lived macOS install with external plugins already configured.

Environment before upgrade:
- OpenClaw `2026.6.11`
- macOS arm64
- Homebrew global install under `/opt/homebrew`
- external plugins present: `openclaw-weixin`, `@openclaw/deepseek-provider`, `@openclaw/tavily-plugin`
- web search configured to use `tavily`
- Tavily API key stored under plugin config

Upgrade flow:

1. Upgrade OpenClaw core to `2026.7.1`
2. Ensure Node is compatible (`v24.18.0` in this repro)
3. Run:
   - `openclaw gateway install`
   - `openclaw gateway start`
4. Observe gateway never becomes ready
5. `openclaw gateway status --deep` shows service loaded/running or restarting, but probe fails / port not truly ready
6. Logs show:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

7. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`
8. Observe the same plugin install metadata conflict remains; gateway still not ready
9. Manually force-uninstall and reinstall the conflicting plugin:
   - `openclaw plugins uninstall openclaw-weixin --force`
   - `openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin`
   - `openclaw plugins registry --refresh`
   - `openclaw gateway restart`
10. Gateway finally becomes healthy
11. Now inspect other external plugins (`deepseek`, `tavily`): installed files are present on disk, but status/index surfaces still show old versions or disabled state
12. Attempt a real Tavily call:

```bash
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --limit 3 --query "OpenClaw 2026.7.1 release notes" --json
```

13. It fails with missing credential error, even though Tavily was previously configured:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

14. Inspect current config vs backup:
   - `tools.web.search.provider` is still `tavily`
   - but `plugins.entries.tavily` is gone
   - and `tavily` is missing from `plugins.allow`
   - backup config still contains the Tavily API key subtree
15. Manually restore the missing config and allowlist entries, restart gateway, rerun the direct search test
16. Tavily search succeeds, but some status surfaces can still report stale install/version drift

### Expected behavior

- A plugin install metadata conflict should not permanently block startup without a supported convergence path.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` should either resolve the conflict or provide a deterministic repair path.
- Manual uninstall/reinstall of one conflicting plugin should not silently remove config/allowlist/credential subtrees for other working plugins.
- If a plugin capability is actually working again, status surfaces should converge and stop reporting stale drift.
- The combined repair path should be idempotent.

### Actual behavior

- Gateway readiness is blocked by a plugin install metadata conflict.
- `doctor --fix` does not converge the state.
- Manual plugin reinstall is required to recover gateway readiness.
- Another plugin (`tavily`) can lose its config entry, allowlist membership, and API-key subtree during the repair sequence.
- After manual config restoration, the capability works again, but some status/index views still report old version drift or disabled state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

macOS arm64

### Install method

npm/Homebrew global install

### Model

MiniMax-M3 (not material to the bug)

### Provider / routing chain

- `minimax-portal` for agent runs
- `tavily` for managed web search
- `openclaw-weixin` channel configured

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway managed via macOS LaunchAgent
- external plugins involved in the repro: `openclaw-weixin`, `deepseek`, `tavily`
- Tavily was previously configured and functioning before repair

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Representative blocking log:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

Representative post-repair Tavily failure:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

Representative successful direct Tavily test only after manual config restoration:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "provider": "tavily"
}
```

State observations during recovery:
- `plugins.entries.tavily` missing from current config
- `tavily` missing from `plugins.allow`
- backup config still contained Tavily `webSearch.apiKey`
- direct capability call worked again only after restoring both config entry and allowlist
- some status surfaces still reported stale Tavily version/install drift after the capability was already working

### Impact and severity

High.

This can leave an upgraded install in a state where:
- gateway will not start
- official repair does not converge state
- user must manually inspect config/state internals
- plugin credentials/config can be silently dropped during recovery
- status surfaces remain misleading even after functional recovery

### Additional information

This seems related to, but not fully covered by, existing plugin metadata conflict/state-drift issues such as:
- #97563
- #97768
- #90418
- #107727

What seems unique here is the full chain:
- plugin metadata conflict blocks startup
- doctor cannot clear it
- manual conflicting-plugin reinstall restores gateway
- another plugin then loses config/allowlist/credentials
- capability works again only after manual config restoration
- status/index can still drift after successful functional recovery

A robust fix likely needs all of the following:
- a deterministic source of truth for external plugin install state
- safe, idempotent reconciliation between legacy install index, SQLite state, config entries, and allowlist
- repair tooling that can restore plugin config references without silently dropping unrelated plugin credentials
- status surfaces that reflect actual loaded/working capability state after recovery

target.title: fix(models): reject oversized piped auth input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readPipedStdin()` helper now enforces a 1 MiB cap (matching the existing `MATRIX_CLI_RECOVERY_KEY_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` and `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` limits). The rejection happens at the stream boundary — during the read loop, not after buffering — so oversized input never reaches auth processing.

The change follows the same buffer-chunk pattern used in the Matrix recovery-key stdin fix (PR #108120): collect `Buffer` chunks, track `totalBytes` per chunk, and throw before the cap is exceeded. Normal TTY and small piped input paths are unchanged.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `readPipedStdin`, `models auth stdin`, `paste-token unbounded` — no same-file or same-problem open PR found.

## User Impact

Piped auth commands now fail with an explicit size error for oversized input instead of buffering unbounded data. Normal interactive entry and direct arguments are unaffected.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12be34c454b75916fcf481916dec7998105820df`

### Format / diff check

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/commands/models/auth.ts src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# exit 0
```

### Real CLI proof (local, Node 24.18.0, `pnpm dev`)

Normal small piped API key reaches auth validation:

```
$ printf 'sk-test123456789\n' | OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
...
Updated config: /tmp/openclaw-test-proof/openclaw.json
Auth profile: openai:manual (openai/api_key)
```

Oversized piped input (1 MiB + 1 byte) rejected at the stdin boundary:

```
$ node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(1048577))' |     OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
Error: Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.
```

### Standalone proof (loopback stream, calls real production function)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-models-auth-stdin-limit.mts

  ok: small piped input does not trigger size rejection
  info: small_error=Failed to update auth profile store; ...
  ok: oversized piped input is rejected
  ok: rejection message is "Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes."
  info: oversized_error=Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

New test "rejects oversized piped auth input before buffering it" verifies the exact error message and confirms no downstream auth mutation.

### Mutation check

Reverted the fix to bare `input += String(chunk)` loop with no cap:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/commands/models/auth.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 39 passed (40)
```

Oversized input passes through to validate() which reports "That does not look like an OpenAI API key." instead of the size rejection. Restored fix → 40/40 pass.

### Not tested

- Full `pnpm build` with dist-based CLI (Node 22.22.0 does not meet the >=22.22.3 requirement)

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Catalog-path coverage proves Tool Search / Code Mode preserves plugin result control.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- 68 focused tests passed across agent-core, embedded-agent, adapter, catalog, session-yield, and Plugin SDK suites.
- Package tests type-check: `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.packages.json`.
- Agent tests type-check: `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents.json`.
- Plugin SDK declaration build passes: `tsconfig.plugin-sdk.dts.json`.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, surface budgets, and export synchronization checks pass.
- Changed TypeScript/JavaScript files pass Oxfmt and Oxlint; `git diff --check` passes.

Prepared with AI assistance.

Closes #109761
